body_en: Catholic bishops accuse Trump White House of turning prayer into campaign photo op
Two bishops express regret after the White House posts photos and video of a prayer with them in the Oval Office

Two Catholic bishops who bowed their heads with Donald Trump in the Oval Office now say they regret it, accusing the White House of turning a private prayer into a campaign photo opportunity before next week’s US elections.

Archbishop Jeffrey Grob of Milwaukee and Bishop William Joensen of Des Moines, who were among the 12 bishops who met administration officials last Thursday, issued separate statements of regret over the weekend.

The fallout stems from the White House quickly posting video and photos of the prayer on social media, captioned as Catholic archbishops and bishops praying with the US president, less than two weeks before the midterm elections on 3 November.

Archbishop Grob issued a statement headlined A Public Apology , in which he said he felt “a heavy sadness” over the pain the images had caused, and that he had heard from people alarmed that he had unwittingly joined a political event on the eve of a national vote.

Others, he said, were hurt because of the effect of Trump’s policies on their families. “We should never have been put in that position by the White House,” wrote Grob, adding that he had harbored reservations and “wish I had heeded them”.
Bishop Joensen wrote that “many things tied to this present Administration” were “blatantly at odds with our Catholic faith”.

He said none of the bishops was unaware the meeting fell close to an election, but insisted that none had intended to endorse a party or candidate. “I wish I had been more shrewd and less simple, like those who exploited our meeting for partisan political purposes.”

Grob said the Heritage Foundation, the conservative thinktank behind the Project 2025 rightwing blueprint for the second Trump administration , arranged the meeting. The bishops, he said, were told it would be a private discussion of immigration enforcement, religious-worker visas and human dignity, with a possible chance to pray privately with the president.

After 90 minutes with domestic policy staff, they were ushered into the Oval Office, handed commemorative tokens and, Grob detailed, directed to stand behind Trump’s desk and pray. Nobody told them a video was being recorded, he said, and they never agreed to its release.

Joensen said officials connected to the White House Faith Office invited him, and that the agenda also covered fertility treatment incentives, abortion-inducing drugs and tax credits for private schools.

Archbishop James Golka of Denver, another participant, told his archdiocese’s publication that he understood why many saw the video as an endorsement but that it was “never my intention”. “I’m heartbroken that people are hurt, and that there are people intentionally using this moment to sow disunity,” he said.

Bishop Scott Bullock of Rapid City told the National Catholic Reporter that a Heritage Foundation representative had invited him and that the US Conference of Catholic Bishops was “not unaware” of the meeting. He did not say who in the leadership knew.

Trump has spent his second term fusing Christian prayers with the machinery of government, creating a White House Faith Office by executive order in February 2025 and, the same month, a justice department-led taskforce to “eradicate anti-Christian bias” in federal agencies.

The president faced criticism in April for posting an AI-generated image on his Truth Social platform depicting himself as a Jesus-like figure. He later deleted the post, and claimed it was “supposed to be me as a doctor making people better”.

At the Pentagon, Pete Hegseth, the US defense secretary, has held Christian worship services (which the Associated Press reports have been led only by evangelicals) and in March prayed for “overwhelming violence” against “those who deserve no mercy” in the Iran war.

And when the Episcopal bishop Mariann Budde urged him at his inauguration prayer service to show mercy toward migrants and LGBTQ+ people, Trump demanded that she and her church apologize, which she in turn rejected .

Archbishop Paul Coakley of Oklahoma City, president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops, has urged Catholics to put faith ahead of politics before the vote. The bishops are due to hold their annual fall assembly in Baltimore in November, about two weeks after the election.
“We are, as ever, a pilgrim people,” Grob wrote. “And that includes bishops,”. He ended his apology with “sincere regret”.
body_zh: 天主教主教指责特朗普白宫将祈祷变成竞选合影
白宫发布与他们一起在椭圆形办公室祈祷的照片和视频后，两位主教表示遗憾
两名在椭圆形办公室与唐纳德·特朗普低头的天主教主教现在表示后悔，指责白宫将私人祈祷变成了下周美国大选前的竞选拍照机会。
密尔沃基大主教杰弗里·格罗布和得梅因主教威廉·乔恩森是上周四会见政府官员的 12 名主教，他们在周末分别发表了遗憾声明。
此事的后果源于白宫在社交媒体上迅速发布了祈祷的视频和照片，标题是天主教大主教和主教与美国总统一起祈祷，当时距离 11 月 3 日中期选举还不到两周。
格罗布大主教发表了一份题为“公开道歉”的声明，他在声明中表示，他对这些图像造成的痛苦感到“沉重的悲伤”，并且他从人们那里得知，他在全国投票前夕无意中参加了一场政治活动，这让他感到震惊。
他说，其他人因为特朗普政策对他们家庭的影响而受到伤害。格罗布写道：“白宫不应该把我们置于这样的境地。”他补充说，他对此持保留态度，“希望我当时能听从他们的意见”。
约恩森主教写道，“与本届政府有关的许多事情”“与我们的天主教信仰公然不一致”。
他说，没有一位主教不知道这次会议临近选举，但坚称没有人打算支持某个政党或候选人。 “我希望自己能更精明一些，不要那么简单，就像那些利用我们的会议来达到党派政治目的的人一样。”
格罗布表示，特朗普第二届政府的“2025计划”右翼蓝图背后的保守派智库传统基金会安排了这次会议。他说，主教们被告知，这将是一次关于移民执法、宗教工作者签证和人类尊严的私下讨论，并有可能有机会与总统私下祈祷。
与国内政策工作人员待了 90 分钟后，他们被带进椭圆形办公室，递上纪念币，格罗布详细介绍说，他们被指示站在特朗普的办公桌后面祈祷。他说，没有人告诉他们正在录制视频，而且他们也从未同意发布该视频。
乔恩森说，与白宫信仰办公室有关的官员邀请了他，议程还包括生育治疗激励措施、堕胎药物和私立学校的税收抵免。
另一位参与者、丹佛大主教詹姆斯·戈尔卡 (James Golka) 告诉他的大主教管区出版物，他理解为什么许多人将这段视频视为认可，但这“从来不是我的本意”。他说：“我对人们受到伤害感到心碎，有人故意利用这个时刻散播不团结的种子。”
拉皮德城的斯科特·布洛克主教告诉国家天主教记者，传统基金会的代表邀请了他，美国天主教主教会议“并非不知道”这次会议。他没有透露领导层中谁知道。
特朗普在第二个任期内将基督教祈祷与政府机制融合在一起，于 2025 年 2 月通过行政命令设立了白宫信仰办公室，并于同月成立了一个由司法部领导的特别工作组，以“消除联邦机构中的反基督教偏见”。
总统四月份因在他的真相社交平台上发布人工智能生成的图像而受到批评，该图像将自己描绘成类似耶稣的人物。他后来删除了该帖子，并声称“我作为一名医生应该让人们变得更好”。
在五角大楼，美国国防部长皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth) 举行了基督教礼拜活动（据美联社报道，这些活动仅由福音派人士主持），并于 3 月份祈祷伊朗战争中“那些不值得怜悯的人”遭受“压倒性的暴力”。
当圣公会主教玛丽安·巴德 (Mariann Budde) 在就职祈祷仪式上敦促他对移民和 LGBTQ+ 人群表示怜悯时，特朗普要求她和她的教会道歉，但遭到她的拒绝。
美国天主教主教会议主席、俄克拉荷马城大主教保罗·科克利敦促天主教徒在投票前将信仰置于政治之上。主教们定于十一月在选举后大约两周在巴尔的摩举行年度秋季大会。
“我们一如既往，是朝圣者，”格罗布写道。 “这包括主教”。他以“真诚的遗憾”结束了道歉。

body_en: Court blocks bid by Trump DoJ to stop California from counting mail-in ballots | US voting rights
Court blocks bid by Trump DoJ to stop California from counting mail-in ballots
California counties were told by DoJ to set aside and verify ballots administration claims belong to noncitizen voters

A ⁠US appeals court on Monday ruled against Donald ⁠Trump’s ​justice department in a major voting dispute ahead ⁠of the midterm elections, denying a ⁠request to block California from ​counting ‌mail ballots ‌from people on a list ‌of more than 20,000 registered voters the federal government alleges are likely noncitizens.

The decision by ‌the San Francisco-based ninth US circuit court of appeals marked the latest setback in Trump’s efforts to assert ⁠a greater federal role in ​overseeing ​elections in ​the run-up to the 3 ​November midterms ​in ​which his fellow Republicans are fighting to retain control of Congress.
On Friday, at least 18 counties across California received letters demanding local election officials set aside and verify ballots that Trump’s administration claims belong to noncitizen voters.
The DoJ’s lawsuit, filed earlier this month, marked the latest escalation in the Trump administration’s battle with California.

body_en: Trump dangles $1m reward for reporting voter fraud in past or upcoming elections | Donald Trump
Trump dangles $1m reward for reporting voter fraud in past or upcoming elections
President’s comments come ahead of November midterm elections and follow his claims of widespread voter fraud
Donald Trump has announced a $1m reward for reports of voter fraud in past elections and the upcoming midterm elections, with payment contingent on the arrest and conviction of those responsible.

In a Truth Social post on Monday, the president wrote: “Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud! Thank you for your attention to this matter.”

Trump later reiterated the offer to reporters before boarding Air Force One for a campaign rally in Mississippi, saying : “I’m also going to be issuing a $1m bonus or reward, or whatever you want to call it, for anybody that reports voter fraud, leading to the arrest and conviction of somebody.”
Trump did not disclose how he plans to pay for the rewards.
The Guardian has reached out to the White House for comment.
Trump’s latest comments come ahead of the November midterm elections and follow his repeated and unfounded claims of widespread voter fraud.

Earlier this month, Democratic state attorneys general expanded coordination efforts to counter potential federal interference in the upcoming elections, amid growing concerns over the administration’s voter fraud claims.
California’s attorney general Rob Bonta criticized the Trump administration’s efforts to restrict alleged noncitizen voting, accusing it of “politicizing and weaponizing the law”.

In 2020, Texas’s Republican lieutenant governor Dan Patrick offered a $25,000 for election-fraud tips, saying at the time: “I support President Trump’s efforts to identify voter fraud in the presidential election and his commitment to making sure that every legal vote is counted and every illegal vote is disqualified.”

Following Patrick’s offer, the first payout went to Eric Frank, a Democratic poll worker in Pennsylvania whose tip led to the conviction of a 72-year-old Republican for voting twice – once in his own name and once in his son’s – the Washington Post reported in 2021.

特朗普悬赏 100 万美元奖励举报过去或即将举行的选举中的选民欺诈行为
总统的评论是在 11 月中期选举之前发表的，此前他还声称存在广泛的选民欺诈行为
唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 宣布悬赏 100 万美元，奖励在过去的选举和即将到来的中期选举中举报选民舞弊的行为，奖励金额取决于责任人的逮捕和定罪。
总统在周一的《真相社会》帖子中写道：“任何举报过去选举或即将到来的 2026 年中期选举中选民欺诈行为的人，一旦逮捕并定罪制造欺诈的人，将获得 1,000,000 美元！感谢您对此事的关注。”
特朗普后来在登上空军一号前往密西西比州参加竞选集会之前向记者重申了这一提议，他说：“我还将向举报选民欺诈、导致某人被捕并定罪的任何人发放 100 万美元的奖金或奖励，或者随便你怎么称呼它。”
特朗普没有透露他计划如何支付这些奖励。
《卫报》已联系白宫请其置评。
特朗普的最新言论是在 11 月中期选举之前发表的，此前他一再毫无根据地声称存在广泛的选民欺诈行为。
本月早些时候，由于对政府选民欺诈指控的担忧日益加剧，民主党州总检察长扩大了协调努力，以应对联邦政府对即将举行的选举的潜在干预。
加州总检察长罗布·邦塔批评特朗普政府限制所谓的非公民投票的努力，指责其“将法律政治化和武器化”。
2020 年，德克萨斯州共和党副州长丹·帕特里克 (Dan Patrick) 悬赏 25,000 美元用于支付选举舞弊举报，当时他表示：“我支持特朗普总统在总统选举中识别选民舞弊行为的努力，以及他确保每张合法选票都被计入、每张非法选票都被取消资格的承诺。”
据《华盛顿邮报》2021 年报道，在帕特里克提出提议后，第一笔款项支付给了宾夕法尼亚州民主党民意调查工作人员埃里克·弗兰克 (Eric Frank)，他的举报导致一名 72 岁的共和党人因两次投票而被定罪——一次以自己的名义，一次以儿子的名义投票。

body_en: Ex-South Carolina governors endorse Democrat Annie Andrews in Senate race | US midterm elections 2026
Ex-South Carolina governors endorse Democrat Annie Andrews in Senate race
Republican and Democrat come together for a rare joint endorsement of candidate in unexpected competitive race
Two South Carolina former governors, David Beasley and Jim Hodges, a Republican and Democrat respectively, have come together for a rare joint endorsement for Democrat Annie Andrews’s Senate bid.

Andrews, a pediatrician, is looking to flip the seat , currently held by Darline Graham, the Trump-endorsed sister of the late senator Lindsey Graham, in what has become an unexpectedly competitive race for the usually reliably red state.

“This country is too divided, and the political rhetoric has gotten way, way out of hand,” says Beasley in the former governors’ joint endorsement video. “That’s why we’re coming together to support Annie Andrews,” says Hodges.
The two former governors, who once faced off against each other, acknowledged that while they don’t agree on everything, they agree on Andrews as the best candidate to put South Carolina first.
“Annie understands that leadership isn’t about making people angrier. Well, it’s about making things better,” says Beasley. “She’s willing to put people ahead of politics,” adds Hodges.
Beasley adds: “We may have served as your governor from different political parties. But we agree South Carolina deserves better than more of the same political fighting.”

Last week, Beasley, a Democrat-turned-Republican who served as governor of the Palmetto State from 1995 to 1999 before losing re-election to Hodges, wrote an opinion piece for the Charleston-based Post and Courier paper, lamenting the state of the party under Donald Trump.

“What has happened in the Republican Party today is just heartbreaking,” he wrote. “Too many in the party have gone along with winning by tearing others down and pitting people and communities against one another … I have yet to see President Donald Trump, as leader of the Republican Party, show compassion or even respect to someone or some group that he disagrees with.
“The vitriol is toxic, and it is undeniably feeding into the hearts, minds and souls of Americans.”
It is “not the party that I knew, and it is not the party that I consider myself a member of”, he added.

Recent polling has indicated that Graham still holds a lead over Andrews, though the nonpartisan Cook Political Report has moved the state in the Democrats’ direction, from “Likely Republican” to “Lean Republican”.

And it isn’t the only time in this year’s midterms that prominent Republicans have crossed party lines and backed Democrats. In usually deep-red Kansas, two former Republican governors, Bill Graves and Mike Hayden, endorsed the Democratic candidate , Adam Hamilton, in his bid to unseat the Republican incumbent, senator Roger Marshall.

In Texas, another unexpected Senate battleground, the Democratic nominee, James Talarico, has received public endorsements from more than 20 Republican leaders , as well as members of the Bush family , over Republican Ken Paxton. There have also been cross-party endorsements from Republicans for Democrats in Georgia , Montana , Florida , Virginia , Illinois and South Dakota .
body_zh: 前南卡罗来纳州州长在参议院竞选中支持民主党人安妮·安德鲁斯2026 年美国中期选举
前南卡罗来纳州州长在参议院竞选中支持民主党人安妮·安德鲁斯
共和党和民主党在意想不到的竞争中罕见地联合支持候选人
两位南卡罗来纳州前州长戴维·比斯利和吉姆·霍奇斯（分别是共和党人和民主党人）罕见地联合支持民主党人安妮·安德鲁斯竞选参议员。
儿科医生安德鲁斯正在寻求翻转目前由已故参议员林赛·格雷厄姆的妹妹达琳·格雷厄姆(Darline Graham)占据的席位，这场对通常可靠的红色州的竞争已经出乎意料地激烈。
“这个国家太过分裂，政治言论已经失控，”比斯利在前州长的联合认可视频中说道。 “这就是我们齐心协力支持安妮·安德鲁斯的原因，”霍奇斯说。
这两位曾经针锋相对的前州长承认，虽然他们并非在所有问题上都达成一致，但他们一致认为安德鲁斯是把南卡罗来纳州放在首位的最佳候选人。
“安妮明白，领导力不是让人们更愤怒。而是让事情变得更好，”比斯利说。 “她愿意把人民置于政治之上，”霍奇斯补充道。
比斯利补充道：“我们可能来自不同的政党担任你们的州长。但我们一致认为，南卡罗来纳州应该得到更好的待遇，而不是更多相同的政治斗争。”
上周，比斯利从民主党转为共和党，曾于 1995 年至 1999 年担任帕尔梅托州州长，但在连任中输给了霍奇斯。他为查尔斯顿的《邮报与信使报》撰写了一篇评论文章，对唐纳德·特朗普领导下的共和党状况表示哀叹。
“共和党今天发生的事情令人心碎，”他写道。 “党内有太多人通过摧毁他人、让人民和社区相互对抗来赢得胜利……我还没有看到唐纳德·特朗普总统作为共和党领袖，对他不同意的某人或某个群体表现出同情甚至尊重。
“尖酸刻薄是有毒的，无可否认，它正在渗透到美国人的心灵、思想和灵魂中。”
他补充说，这“不是我所认识的政党，也不是我认为自己是其中成员的政党”。
最近的民意调查显示，格雷厄姆仍然领先安德鲁斯，尽管无党派的库克政治报告已将该州推向民主党的方向，从“可能是共和党”变为“倾向共和党”。
这并不是今年中期选举中共和党知名人士唯一一次跨越党派界限支持民主党。在通常深红色的堪萨斯州，两位前共和党州长比尔·格雷夫斯和迈克·海登支持民主党候选人亚当·汉密尔顿，以推翻共和党现任参议员罗杰·马歇尔。
在德克萨斯州，另一个意想不到的参议院战场，民主党候选人詹姆斯·塔拉里科(James Talarico)获得了20多位共和党领导人以及布什家族成员的公开支持，而不是共和党人肯·帕克斯顿(Ken Paxton)。佐治亚州、蒙大拿州、佛罗里达州、弗吉尼亚州、伊利诺伊州和南达科他州的共和党人也对民主党人表示跨党派支持。

summary: Comey, an outspoken critic of Donald Trump, accused of leaking information related to US national defense The justice department charged former FBI director James Comey on Monday with two counts of leaking information related to national defense, the third tim
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普直言不讳的批评者科米被指控泄露与美国国防相关的信息 司法部指控前联邦调查局局长
body_en: Justice department charges ex-FBI director James Comey for third time | James Comey
Justice department charges ex-FBI director James Comey for third time
Comey, an outspoken critic of Donald Trump, accused of leaking information related to US national defense

The justice department charged former FBI director James Comey on Monday with two counts of leaking information related to national defense, the third time the Trump administration has filed criminal charges against one of Donald Trump’s most despised foes.

The charges, filed in federal court in Washington DC, provide few details about what Comey is alleged to have leaked. The government alleges that the former FBI director leaked the information in 2016 and conspired with an unnamed person to give the information to a national news outlet.

Patrick Fitzgerald, Comey’s attorney, said the charges were related to a 5 October 2016 New York Times article that had already been investigated by prosecutors. The case was filed through a criminal maneuver known as an “information” – meaning it was not approved by a grand jury. While prosecutors will eventually have to have the charges approved by a grand jury, filing the charges through an information appears to have been an effort to quickly get the criminal charges in against Comey before the 10-year statute of limitations expires.

“Ten years after the article was published, the government filed an ‘information’ against Mr Comey that was not approved by a judge nor issued by a grand jury. It purports to charge Mr Comey with crimes he did not commit,” Fitzgerald said in a statement.

In a court filing unsealed on Monday , Comey’s lawyers argued the indictment should be dismissed because the statute of limitations had expired and it had been twice investigated and determined no charges should be filed. They also argued that the law required an indictment, not an information, within the 10-year statute of limitations.

Trump fired Comey in 2017 as he worked on an investigation into whether Trump allies colluded with Russia during the 2016 presidential election. The former FBI director has since become an outspoken critic of the president.

Last year, the justice department charged Comey with lying to Congress, but the charges were thrown out after a judge found the prosecutor handling the case, a White House ally installed to bring the case, was unlawfully appointed.

Earlier this year, the justice department filed charges against Comey in federal court in North Carolina for posting a picture of a formation of seashells spelling out “8647” – which for some people is a shorthand way of saying get rid of Trump. Legal experts have said that case is thin.
“Well, they’re back again. It would almost be funny if wasn’t such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice. One that we cannot become numb to,” Comey said in a video posted online.
body_zh: 司法部第三次指控前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米詹姆斯·科米
司法部第三次指控前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米
唐纳德·特朗普的直言不讳的批评者科米被指控泄露与美国国防有关的信息
司法部周一指控前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米犯有两项泄露国防相关信息的罪名，这是特朗普政府第三次对唐纳德·特朗普最受鄙视的敌人之一提起刑事指控。
这些向华盛顿特区联邦法院提起的指控并未提供有关科米据称泄露的内容的细节。政府声称，前联邦调查局局长于 2016 年泄露了该信息，并与一名未透露姓名的人合谋将该信息提供给一家全国性新闻媒体。
科米的律师帕特里克·菲茨杰拉德 (Patrick Fitzgerald) 表示，这些指控与 2016 年 10 月 5 日《纽约时报》的一篇文章有​​关，检察官已对该文章进行了调查。该案是通过一种被称为“信息”的刑事手段提起的——这意味着它没有得到大陪审团的批准。虽然检察官最终必须让大陪审团批准这些指控，但通过信息提出指控似乎是为了在 10 年诉讼时效到期之前迅速对科米提出刑事指控。
“这篇文章发表十年后，政府提交了一份针对科米先生的‘信息’，该信息未经法官批准，也未经大陪审团发布。它旨在指控科米先生犯下他没有犯下的罪行，”菲茨杰拉德在一份声明中说。
在周一启封的一份法庭文件中，科米的律师辩称，起诉书应该被驳回，因为诉讼时效已过，而且已经过两次调查，并确定不应提出指控。他们还辩称，法律要求在 10 年诉讼时效内提出起诉，而不是提供信息。
特朗普于 2017 年解雇了科米，当时科米正在调查特朗普的盟友是否在 2016 年总统选举期间与俄罗斯勾结。这位前联邦调查局局长此后成为总统的直言不讳的批评者。
去年，司法部指控科米向国会撒谎，但在一名法官发现处理此案的检察官（一位负责提起此案的白宫盟友）被非法任命后，这些指控被驳回。
今年早些时候，司法部向北卡罗来纳州联邦法院对科米提出指控，因为科米发布了一张贝壳排列的照片，上面写着“8647”——对某些人来说，这是“除掉特朗普”的简写方式。法律专家表示，此案案情薄弱。
“好吧，他们又回来了。如果不是司法部如此令人震惊的滥用职权，那就太有趣了。我们不能对此麻木不仁，”科米在网上发布的视频中说道。

title_en: Lula mobilized millions to win Brazil's election, while Bolsonaro contests loss and Trump cries foul
title_zh: 卢拉动员数百万人赢得巴西大选，而博尔索纳罗则对失败提出异议，特朗普则大声疾呼
summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won reelection in Brazil's presidential runoff
summary_zh: 巴西总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦在巴西总统决选中赢得连任
body_en: Lula mobilized millions to win Brazil's election, while Bolsonaro contests loss and Trump cries foul
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won reelection in Brazil's presidential runoff
By ANNA-CATHERINE BRIGIDA Associated Press and MAURICIO SAVARESE Associated Press

WASHINGTON -- President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ’s comeback to win Brazil’s presidential runoff Sunday is already facing its first hurdle as his competitor, Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro , challenges the results, setting the stage for a possible showdown between the country’s two polarizing political forces.

Lula, who convinced an extra 10.4 million voters to support him in the runoff, is expected to take office on Jan. 5, 2027, for his fourth non-consecutive term. He will serve as a counterweight in a region where leaders are shifting to the right and aligning with U.S. President Donald Trump. Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, promised to cozy up to the Trump administration.
President Donald Trump suggested on Monday, without providing evidence, that Lula’s reelection was “rigged.”

“Elections have to be indisputable and it looked very bad to me,” Trump told reporters before flying to Mississippi for a rally. He added, “I thought it had a very bad look, the way it was tabulated.”
Trump also said: “It looked like another rigged election, frankly.”

At a news conference Sunday, Bolsonaro said he planned to request an annulment of the election following a chaotic extension of voting at the request of both candidates. However, it's unclear what legal avenue he would have to do that. His father, now serving a 27-year sentence for a coup attempt, unsuccessfully contested his loss to Lula four years ago. Flavio Bolsonaro visited his father, who is under house arrest, on Monday, the younger Bolsonaro's public relations office said.
Early signs from Brazil’s institutions and from leaders across the region, including conservative presidents who oppose Lula, suggest the results will be respected nationally and internationally.
Even with the vote extension, Lula’s win was decisive. The soon-to-be 81-year-old incumbent won more than 64 million votes compared to just under 60 million for Bolsonaro, a margin of nearly 4%.
President of Brazil’s electoral authority, Kassio Nunes, who was appointed to the Supreme Court by ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, was among those who recognized Lula’s victory Sunday.

“This is a really uphill battle for Flavio Bolsonaro. Important Brazilian power brokers are closing ranks behind Lula, sometimes begrudgingly," said Brian Winter, Brazil analyst and editor-in-chief of Americas Quarterly.
“I sense that Brazilian power brokers that matter don’t really want to go down the path of a truly contested election,” he said.

The key to Lula’s win was the additional 14.1 million voters who showed up for the second-round election, including those who voted for other candidates in the first round. Analysts say three-quarters of those votes went to Lula, handing him the victory. And notably, the first round set a record for the number of Brazilians who decided not to vote, while the second round had the least number of abstentions ever.

Lula gave his digital campaign to lawmaker André Janones, who mounted a fierce and persistent social media operation that mobilized many of those previously uncommitted voters. Janones' key tool was a channel on messaging app WhatsApp called “Lula's Army,” which gathered almost 11 million people and mobilized them to campaign via social media for the incumbent.

Janones “basically embraced the right’s style of aggressive politics, very intense, constant messaging,” said Oliver Stuenkel, a professor of International Relations at Fundação Getulio Vargas in Sao Paulo.
“The defeat in the first round jolted the Lula campaign into action. The strategy during the first round was lackluster and saw a lot of infighting,” Stuenkel said.

Juliano Cortinhas, international relations professor at the University of Brasília, said Lula's social media initiative in the runoff was also key to pressuring Meta, the owner of Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook, to end what the president's campaign denounced as bias helping Bolsonaro.
Brazil’s top electoral court ruled on Oct.15 that Meta must adopt measures that assure equal treatment of the two presidential candidates, which the company later said it addressed.
body_zh: 卢拉动员数百万人赢得巴西大选，而博尔索纳罗则对失败提出异议，特朗普则大声疾呼
巴西总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦在巴西总统决选中赢得连任
安娜-凯瑟琳·布里吉达 美联社和毛里西奥·萨瓦雷塞 美联社
华盛顿——巴西总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦周日在巴西总统决选中复出，但他的竞争对手、参议员弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗对结果提出了挑战，这已经面临第一个障碍，这为该国两股两极分化的政治力量之间可能的摊牌奠定了基础。
卢拉在决选中说服了额外 1,040 万选民支持他，预计将于 2027 年 1 月 5 日就职，这是他的第四个非连续任期。他将成为该地区领导人右倾并与美国总统唐纳德·特朗普结盟的制衡力量。前总统博尔索纳罗的儿子博尔索纳罗承诺会讨好特朗普政府。
唐纳德·特朗普总统周一在没有提供证据的情况下暗示卢拉的连任是“被操纵的”。
“选举必须是无可争议的，但对我来说，这看起来非常糟糕，”特朗普在飞往密西西比州参加集会之前告诉记者。他补充道，“我认为它的表格看起来非常糟糕。”
特朗普还表示：“坦率地说，这看起来像是另一场被操纵的选举。”
在周日的新闻发布会上，博尔索纳罗表示，应两位候选人的要求，在混乱地延长投票后，他计划要求废除选举。然而，目前尚不清楚他必须通过什么法律途径才能做到这一点。他的父亲因政变未遂而被判 27 年徒刑，目前正在服刑，四年前，他对输给卢拉的竞选提出了异议，但没有成功。小博尔索纳罗的公共关系办公室表示，弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗周一探望了被软禁的父亲。
巴西机构和该地区领导人（包括反对卢拉的保守派总统）的初步迹象表明，选举结果将受到国内和国际的尊重。
即使投票延期，卢拉的胜利也是决定性的。这位即将81岁的现任总统赢得了超过6400万张选票，而博尔索纳罗赢得了不到6000万张选票，差距接近4%。
巴西选举当局主席卡西奥·努内斯（Kassio Nunes）是周日承认卢拉获胜的人之一，他被前总统雅伊尔·博尔索纳罗（Jair Bolsonaro）任命为最高法院法官。
“对于弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗来说，这确实是一场艰苦的战斗。巴西重要的权力掮客正在向卢拉靠拢，有时甚至是不情愿的，”巴西分析师兼《美洲季刊》主编布莱恩·温特(Brian Winter)表示。
“我感觉巴西重要的权力掮客并不真的想走上真正有争议的选举之路，”他说。
卢拉获胜的关键在于参加第二轮选举的额外1410万选民，其中包括在第一轮投票给其他候选人的选民。分析人士称，其中四分之三的选票投给了卢拉，使他获得了胜利。值得注意的是，第一轮决定不投票的巴西人数创下了纪录，而第二轮则有有史以来最少的弃权票。
卢拉将他的数字竞选活动交给了立法者安德烈·雅诺内斯，后者发起了一场激烈而持久的社交媒体行动，动员了许多以前未表态的选民。贾诺内斯的关键工具是通讯应用程序 WhatsApp 上一个名为“卢拉军队”的频道，该频道聚集了近 1100 万人，并动员他们通过社交媒体为现任总统竞选。
圣保罗 Getulio Vargas 基金会国际关系教授奥利弗·斯图恩克尔 (Oliver Stuenkel) 表示，雅诺内斯“基本上接受了右翼激进的政治风格，非常强烈、持续不断地传递信息”。
“第一轮的失败让卢拉竞选活动陷入了困境。第一轮的策略乏善可陈，出现了很多内讧，”斯图恩克尔说。
巴西利亚大学国际关系教授朱利亚诺·科蒂尼亚斯表示，卢拉在决选中的社交媒体倡议也是向 Instagram、WhatsApp 和 Facebook 的所有者梅塔施压的关键，要求梅塔结束总统竞选团队谴责的帮助博尔索纳罗的偏见。
巴西最高选举法院于 10 月 15 日裁定，Meta 必须采取措施确保两位总统候选人受到平等待遇，该公司后来表示已解决这一问题。

title_en: Judge says DOJ illegally fired the daughter of former FBI director Comey
title_zh: 法官称司法部非法解雇前联邦调查局局长科米的女儿
summary: Maurene Comey served as a federal prosecutor in Manhattan for around a decade. A judicial ruling finding her dismissal unlawful adds to concerns of politically motivated firings at the DOJ.
summary_zh: 莫林·科米在曼哈顿担任联邦检察官约十年。司法裁决认定解雇她非法，加剧了员工的担忧
body_en: Maurene Comey was illegally fired from DOJ, judge finds : NPR

Maurene Comey was illegally fired from DOJ, judge finds Maurene Comey served as a federal prosecutor in Manhattan for around a decade. A judicial ruling finding her dismissal unlawful adds to concerns of politically motivated firings at the DOJ.
Judge says DOJ illegally fired the daughter of former FBI director Comey
Maurene Comey (R), daughter of former FBI Director James Comey, departs a courthouse in October 2025 in Alexandria, Va. Win McNamee/Getty Images hide caption
A New York federal judge ruled Monday that the Justice Department unlawfully fired former prosecutor Maurene Comey, who is the daughter of ex-FBI Director James Comey .

Maurene Comey served as a federal prosecutor in Manhattan for around a decade, working on high-profile cases against defendants like Sean "Diddy" Combs, Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell. The Trump Justice Department fired her in July 2025 despite her consistently receiving accolades from the department for her work.

In response, she sued the Justice Department and others, arguing that her dismissal was unlawful and unconstitutional. Her lawsuit said she was fired because her father is the former FBI director, a prominent critic of President Trump.
Grand jury indicts former FBI director James Comey for a second time

The Justice Department has twice indicted the elder Comey. The first case was dismissed. The second prosecution, which is still pending, accuses him of threatening the president in a photo of seashells posted on social media.

In his ruling Monday, U.S. District Judge Jesse Furman, a nominee of former President Barack Obama, wrote that the Department of Justice " invented a new and expansive theory of executive power " in dismissing Maurene Comey, and violated her constitutional right to due process.
"To accept Defendants' argument would be to unsettle the very equilibrium established by this Nation's constitutional system," the judge wrote.

The opinion adds to concerns of politically motivated dismissals at the DOJ. Several federal prosecutors and former FBI agents have sued the DOJ under the Trump administration over their dismissals, alleging that they were fired for political reasons tied to their work.
Former federal prosecutor is suing DOJ for 'unlawful and retaliatory' firing
Comey's lawyers praised Monday's ruling, and said it reaffirms that the president must comply with the law as part of the Constitution's checks and balances.
"This hard-earned victory belongs to Ms. Comey, to all civil servants, and to all fighting for the rule of law," her attorneys said in a statement.
The judge's ruling calls for Comey to receive back pay dating to when she was fired last year, and for her to return as a prosecutor to the Southern District of New York, if she so chooses.
The Justice Department said it disagreed with the decision, and would appeal in due course.

The court's order is not final. Judge Furman did yet not rule on Maurene Comey's First Amendment argument that she was fired for politically protected speech, and plans to hear further briefings on that claim.

法官称司法部非法解雇前联邦调查局局长科米的女儿
前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米的女儿莫琳·科米（右）于 2025 年 10 月离开弗吉尼亚州亚历山大的法院。Win McNamee/Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
纽约一名联邦法官周一裁定，司法部非法解雇前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米的女儿莫琳·科米。
莫琳·科米 (Maurene Comey) 在曼哈顿担任联邦检察官约十年，负责针对肖恩·“老爹”库姆斯、杰弗里·爱泼斯坦和吉斯莱恩·麦克斯韦等被告的备受瞩目的案件。尽管她的工作不断获得司法部的赞誉，但特朗普司法部还是于 2025 年 7 月解雇了她。
作为回应，她起诉司法部和其他机构，称解雇她是非法且违宪的。她的诉讼称，她被解雇是因为她的父亲是前联邦调查局局长，也是特朗普总统的著名批评者。
大陪审团第二次起诉前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米
司法部已两次起诉老科米。第一个案件被驳回。第二项起诉仍在审理中，指控他在社交媒体上发布贝壳照片威胁总统。
前总统巴拉克·奥巴马的提名人、美国地区法官杰西·弗曼在周一的裁决中写道，司法部在解雇莫琳·科米时“发明了一种新的、广泛的行政权力理论”，侵犯了她享有正当程序的宪法权利。
法官写道：“接受被告的论点将破坏这个国家宪法制度所建立的平衡。”
该意见加剧了人们对司法部出于政治动机的解雇的担忧。几名联邦检察官和前联邦调查局特工就特朗普政府领导下的解雇起诉司法部，声称他们因与工作相关的政治原因而被解雇。
前联邦检察官起诉司法部“非法和报复性”解雇
科米的律师对周一的裁决表示赞赏，并表示该裁决重申总统必须遵守法律，作为宪法制衡的一部分。
“这一来之不易的胜利属于科米女士、属于所有公务员以及所有为法治而奋斗的人，”她的律师在一份声明中表示。
法官的裁决要求科米收回去年她被解雇时的欠薪，并要求她返回纽约南区担任检察官，如果她愿意的话。
司法部表示不同意这一决定，并将在适当时候提出上诉。
法院的命令不是最终的。弗曼法官尚未对莫琳·科米的第一修正案论点做出裁决，即她因受政治保护的言论而被解雇，并计划听取有关该主张的进一步简报。

body_en: Trump heads to Mississippi as the two parties prepare for final sprint ahead of midterm Election Day

President Donald Trump is heading to Mississippi, as he continues a closing midterm campaign blitz that highlights Republicans’ challenges ahead of an election that could drastically shift power in Washington and statehouses across the country
By BILL BARROW Associated Press and SOPHIE BATES Associated Press

CORINTH, Miss. -- President Donald Trump heads Monday to Mississippi, as he continues a closing midterm campaign blitz that highlights Republicans' challenges ahead of an election that could drastically shift power in Washington and statehouses across the country.

Mississippi, among the nation's most reliably Republican states, is not where the GOP envisioned needing a late-October stop from the president. But GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith faces a stiff challenge from Scott Colom, one of many Democratic underdogs that have managed to expand the House and Senate battleground maps because of widespread voter discontent over inflation, the Iran war and other aspects of Trump’s second presidency.

The evening rally with Hyde-Smith will kick off a week that continues to pit Trump against former President Barack Obama , the Democrat he first succeeded in 2017, and former Vice President Kamala Harris , the Democrat he defeated in 2024 to return to power. Trump's itinerary has been taking him to many states that he won comfortably in 2024.

Other top nominees and surrogates are greeting voters — almost 30 million of whom have already cast ballots — as Republicans scramble to protect their threadbare majority in the House, shore up a Senate majority that was once thought secure and maintain the GOP's national advantage in state capitals.

Harris will campaign in Wisconsin with Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, who faces Rep. Tom Tiffany, a Trump ally, for governor. Crowley would be the state's first Black governor if elected to lead the battleground state.

In Georgia, Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff and gubernatorial nominee Keisha Lance Bottoms are getting an assist from Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, chairman of the Democratic Governors' Association and a likely 2028 presidential candidate, two days after Trump made his second October visit to the state.

Minnesota will be a center of the progressive movement's effort to leverage many Americans' economic struggles. Democratic Senate nominee Peggy Flanagan, the current lieutenant governor, is welcoming House Progressive Caucus Chairwoman Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., to advocate for a national health insurance plan to achieve universal coverage.

House Democrats also continue to expand their spending footprint, with the House Majority PAC announcing almost $2.5 million in new spending in Minnesota and Indiana districts that had been considered solid GOP territory earlier in the cycle. The Minnesota seat is a heavily rural and small-town district that has been reliably Republican for generations, other than a recent stretch when Tim Walz, the state's two-term governor and Democrats' 2024 vice presidential nominee, represented the sprawling district.
But it's Trump's visit to Mississippi that perhaps brings the midterm landscape into the sharpest relief with just a week of campaigning left before votes are tallied.
To be sure, Hyde-Smith, who is vying for her second full term, remains the favorite in a state Trump won three times by an average of nearly 20 percentage points.

But Colom, a local prosecutor who would make history Mississippi's first Black senator since post-Civil War Reconstruction, is looking to parlay inflation, Trump's lagging popularity and Hyde-Smith's mistakes into an upset.
Trump told DOJ to sue to block Alaska Senate results if Republican narrowly loses
Amy Acton says Trump, Vance should 'look at the facts' after Ramaswamy attack ad
Britt McHenry resigns from State Department after basketball game altercation

Colom has outpaced Hyde-Smith in fundraising since he launched his campaign last year, and he caught national attention this month with an ad that played off Hyde-Smith, a former state agriculture commissioner, dismissing beef prices, driven higher by Trump's tariffs and fuel spikes resulting from the Iran war. The ad features Hyde-Smith saying that consumers “have so many other proteins to choose from,” followed by several characters, and then Colom, saying Mississippi should “pick another senator instead.”

Colom's campaign followed with a social media video that featured an AI-generated Hyde-Smith dodging questions about that controversy and other issues. The Democrat took down the video after the Mississippi attorney general said it could violate state law barring the use of deepfakes so close to Election Day.

Senate Democrats’ super PAC, meanwhile, has been a late entry in the contest , with a $1.2 million investment — a paltry sum compared to Senate contests in more populous states like Texas or Georgia but an amount that can go farther in Mississippi’s smaller television markets.
body_zh: 特朗普前往密西西比州，两党为中期选举日之前的最后冲刺做准备
唐纳德·特朗普总统将前往密西西比州，继续结束中期竞选闪电战，突显共和党在选举前面临的挑战，这场选举可能会彻底改变华盛顿和全国各州议会的权力
比尔·巴罗 (BILL BARROW) 美联社和索菲·贝茨 (SOPHIE BATES) 美联社报道
密西西比州科林斯——唐纳德·特朗普总统周一前往密西西比州，继续结束中期竞选闪电战，突显共和党在选举前面临的挑战，这场选举可能会彻底改变华盛顿和全国各州议会的权力。
密西西比州是全国最可靠的共和党州之一，共和党并不认为总统需要在 10 月底停下来。但共和党参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯面临来自斯科特·科洛姆的严峻挑战。斯科特·科洛姆是众多民主党失败者之一，由于选民对通货膨胀、伊朗战争和特朗普第二任总统的其他方面普遍不满，这些失败者设法扩大了参众两院的战场版图。
与海德-史密斯的晚间集会将拉开特朗普与前总统巴拉克·奥巴马(Barack Obama)和前副总统卡马拉·哈里斯(Kamala Harris)的一周的序幕。巴拉克·奥巴马是他在2017年首次成功当选的民主党人，而前副总统卡马拉·哈里斯是他在2024年击败的民主党人，重新掌权。特朗普的行程已经带他去了许多他在 2024 年轻松获胜的州。
其他顶级提名人和代理人正在迎接选民——其中近 3000 万人已经投票——共和党人正忙着保护自己在众议院的微弱多数，巩固一度被认为稳固的参议院多数席位，并维持共和党在各州首府的国家优势。
哈里斯将与密尔沃基县行政长官大卫·克劳利一起在威斯康星州竞选州长，后者将与特朗普盟友众议员汤姆·蒂芙尼竞争。如果当选领导这个战场州，克劳利将成为该州第一位黑人州长。
在佐治亚州，民主党参议员乔恩·奥索夫 (Jon Ossoff) 和州长候选人凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms) 得到了肯塔基州州长安迪·贝希尔 (Andy Beshear) 的协助，安迪·贝希尔是民主党州长协会主席，可能是 2028 年总统候选人，距离特朗普 10 月第二次访问该州两天后。
明尼苏达州将成为进步运动的中心，努力利用许多美国人的经济困境。民主党参议院候选人、现任副州长佩吉·弗拉纳根 (Peggy Flanagan) 欢迎众议院进步党核心小组主席、华盛顿州民主党人普拉米拉·贾亚帕尔 (Pramila Jayapal) 倡导一项国家医疗保险计划，以实现全民覆盖。
众议院民主党人也继续扩大他们的支出足迹，众议院多数派政治行动委员会宣布在明尼苏达州和印第安纳州地区增加近 250 万美元的新支出，这些地区在本周期早些时候被认为是共和党的坚实领土。明尼苏达州的选区是一个以农村和小镇为主的选区，几代人以来一直是共和党的可靠选区，除了最近一段时间，该州两届州长、民主党 2024 年副总统候选人蒂姆·沃尔兹 (Tim Walz) 代表这个庞大的选区。
但特朗普对密西西比州的访问或许让中期选举形势最为明显，因为距离计票仅剩一周的竞选活动。
可以肯定的是，正在争夺第二个完整任期的海德-史密斯仍然是特朗普三次获胜的州的热门人选，平均支持率接近20个百分点。
但科洛姆是一位当地检察官，他将成为密西西比州自内战重建以来第一位黑人参议员，他正在寻求利用通货膨胀、特朗普落后的支持率和海德史密斯的错误来解决这一问题。
特朗普告诉司法部，如果共和党以微弱优势落败，将提起诉讼以阻止阿拉斯加州参议院的结果
艾米·阿克顿表示特朗普和万斯在拉马斯瓦米攻击广告后应该“看看事实”
布里特·麦克亨利因篮球比赛争吵而辞去国务院职务
自从去年发起竞选活动以来，科罗姆在筹款方面已经超过了海德-史密斯，本月他的一则广告引起了全国关注，该广告与前州农业专员海德-史密斯进行了对比，他否认特朗普关税和伊朗战争导致的燃料价格上涨导致牛肉价格上涨。广告中海德史密斯说消费者“有很多其他蛋白质可供选择”，后面是几个人物，然后是科洛姆，说密西西比州应该“选择另一位参议员”。
科罗姆的竞选活动随后发布了一段社交媒体视频，其中人工智能生成的海德史密斯回避了有关这场争议和其他问题的问题。在密西西比州总检察长表示该视频可能违反州法律禁止在临近选举日使用深度伪造品的州法律后，民主党人删除了该视频。
与此同时，参议院民主党的超级政治行动委员会在这场竞争中姗姗来迟，投资了 120 万美元——与德克萨斯州或佐治亚州等人口较多的州的参议院竞选相比，这个数字微不足道，但在密西西比州规模较小的电视市场上，这一数额可以走得更远。

body_en: Trump calls Bill Maher a ‘total loser’ in 1,300-word Truth Social rant | Donald Trump
Trump calls Bill Maher a ‘total loser’ in 1,300-word Truth Social rant
Trump lashes out on Maher after the host interviewed former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt
Donald Trump launched a 1,300-word social media rant against the late-night US TV host Bill Maher on Sunday evening, calling him a “TOTAL LOSER” in a fresh assault on the media.

“Let’s talk about this COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER, Bill Maher ,” the US president wrote. “He’s got a Low Rated Show on equally Low Rated HBO, which was once, long ago, a Network of Quality and Excitement – But that’s all gone.”
Trump’s lengthy and detailed post about Maher came after the host interviewed Karoline Leavitt, the former White House press secretary, on his program Real Time with Bill Maher.
Maher asked Leavitt about Trump’s “lame duck” presidency and whether the president would act on “vengeance” if Republicans largely lose to Democrats in next week’s midterms.

“I worry that if this election goes as badly as it looks like it’s going to go for him and the Republicans, we’re going to have a guy who doesn’t have as much power as he did … and we know he likes vengeance,” Maher told Leavitt.
But Leavitt remained steadfast in her support for Trump and expressed confidence that Republicans could still outperform expectations.
Trump called Maher a “coward who is afraid to tell the truth about how well our Country is running”, claiming that Maher praised him behind the scenes but on television insults him with jokes.

“Also, turn your Laugh Machine off, it’s a joke when they laugh uncontrollably, even when you say nothing funny, and I’m going to have the Republicans not cover you anymore, because they try to talk about you as a guy who is transformative,” Trump wrote.

Trump has previously insulted late-night hosts and comedians on his platform and taken personal offense at those who make him the punchline. Earlier this year, Trump called for Jimmy Kimmel’s show to be terminated after the ABC late-night host joked about Melania Trump. Last year, the US president also called for Seth Meyers to be fired.
But Trump’s lengthy attack on Maher is notable, coming just about a week until the US midterm elections, where Republicans are trying to fend off challenges from Democratic opponents.
The US president chose to launch a tirade against Maher as public polling shows Americans are growing increasingly unhappy with Trump ’s handling of the US economy, cost of living and war with Iran.

But Trump chose to dispute several specific talking points Maher made on his show, including the host’s comments about the justice department’s efforts to target ballots they claim were cast by noncitizens in California , rumors that Trump is turning the White House press briefing room into a swimming pool and Trump’s endorsement of Republican candidates in the upcoming midterms.

Maher, who has been described as a moderate liberal , has dined with Trump on two occasions during the US president’s second administration. Maher has shared his experience with Trump on his HBO show.

Among other insults Trump launched at Maher, he accused the host of drinking a lot of alcohol when they dined together, being a “POTHEAD”, not being nice and catering to a base of viewers who “don’t like working”.

特朗普在 1300 字的真相社会咆哮中称比尔·马赫是“彻头彻尾的失败者”
在主持人采访前白宫新闻秘书卡罗琳·莱维特后，特朗普猛烈抨击马赫
周日晚上，唐纳德·特朗普在社交媒体上对美国深夜电视主持人比尔·马赫发起了长达 1300 字的咆哮，称他是“彻底的失败者”，这是对媒体的新一轮攻击。
“让我们来谈谈这个彻底的失败者，比尔·马赫，”美国总统写道。 “他在同样低收视率的 HBO 上播出了一部低收视率的节目，很久以前，HBO 曾经是一个高质量和令人兴奋的网络——但那一切都消失了。”
特朗普发表了关于马赫的冗长而详细的帖子，此前主持人在他的节目《与比尔·马赫实时对话》中采访了前白宫新闻秘书卡罗琳·莱维特。
马赫向莱维特询问特朗普的“跛脚鸭”总统任期，以及如果共和党在下周的中期选举中大部分输给民主党，总统是否会采取“报复”行动。
马赫告诉莱维特：“我担心，如果这次选举进展得像他和共和党所希望的那样糟糕，我们将迎来一个没有他那么大权力的人……而且我们知道他喜欢复仇。”
但莱维特仍然坚定支持特朗普，并表示相信共和党仍能超出预期。
特朗普称马赫是“胆小鬼，害怕说出我们国家运行情况的真相”，并声称马赫在幕后赞扬他，但在电视上却用笑话侮辱他。
特朗普写道：“还有，把你的笑机关掉，当他们无法控制地大笑时，即使你说的没什么好笑的，这也是个笑话，我不会让共和党人再报道你，因为他们试图把你说成是一个具有变革性的人。”
特朗普此前曾在他的平台上侮辱深夜主持人和喜剧演员，并对那些让他成为笑点的人进行人身攻击。今年早些时候，在美国广播公司深夜主持人拿梅拉尼娅·特朗普开玩笑后，特朗普呼吁终止吉米·金梅尔的节目。去年，美国总统还呼吁解雇塞斯·迈耶斯。
但特朗普对马赫的长时间攻击值得注意，距离美国中期选举仅一周左右，共和党人正试图抵御民主党对手的挑战。
美国总统选择对马赫进行长篇大论，因为公众民意调查显示，美国人对特朗普处理美国经济、生活成本和与伊朗战争的方式越来越不满。
但特朗普选择对马赫在节目中提出的几个具体话题提出异议，包括主持人对司法部针对他们声称是由加州非公民投票的努力的评论、有关特朗普将白宫新闻发布会室变成游泳池的传言，以及特朗普在即将到来的中期选举中对共和党候选人的支持。
马赫被称为温和自由派，在美国总统第二届执政期间曾两次与特朗普共进晚餐。马赫在他的 HBO 节目中分享了他与特朗普的经历。
特朗普对马赫发起的其他侮辱包括，他指责主持人一起用餐时喝了很多酒，是个“笨蛋”，不友善，迎合了一群“不喜欢工作”的观众。

Blanche says Trump isn't trying to meddle with Alaska election results by suing over Senate race
Attorney General Todd Blanche is defending the Trump administration’s lawsuit to block certification of Alaska's Senate results if incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan loses the race

WASHINGTON -- WASHINGTON (AP) — Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday defended the Trump administration's lawsuit to block certification of Alaska's Senate results if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan loses the race and argued that the legal challenge was a necessary step to avoid confusing voters in the closely watched midterm race .

President Donald Trump , who said Friday that he was "the one that said do it,” is not trying to overturn state election results “in any way, shape or form” on the cusp of the Nov. 3 election, Blanche told CNN's “State of the Union.”
“We wish that we didn’t have to do this. We hope for a resolution that works,” Blanche said.

Republicans fear that a second candidate on the ballot who is named Dan Sullivan — a retired teacher and school administrator from the tiny fishing community of Petersburg — could siphon away votes from the senator and tip the outcome in favor of Democrat Mary Peltola , a former congresswoman.

A day after the lawsuit was filed on Thursday, Peltola called it “just flagrant, flagrant corruption in my opinion” and a diversion tactic by Republicans. Alaska’s other Republican senator, Lisa Murkowski, also criticized the lawsuit in a social media post.
Trump told reporters on Sunday that he believed the ballot was illegal because it was unfair and that Sen. Sullivan should be identified to voters as the sitting senator.
“At least let him use the name Sen. Dan Sullivan as opposed to incumbent, because a lot of people don’t know what incumbent means,” Trump said.
Alaskan voters will see “Dan S. Sullivan” identified as a “registered Republican” and “incumbent” on their ballots, while “Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.” will not have a party affiliation.

Blanche represented Trump as a personal attorney before the Republican president appointed him to lead the Department of Justice, which filed the lawsuit in Alaska. Blanche defended Trump in his election inference case before voters elected Trump to a second White House term, effectively ending the criminal prosecution.
Trump told DOJ to sue to block Alaska Senate results if Republican narrowly loses
Amy Acton says Trump, Vance should 'look at the facts' after Ramaswamy attack ad
Britt McHenry resigns from State Department after basketball game altercation

Blanche told CNN host Dana Bash that it was “crazy” for her to ask him if Trump was trying to lay the groundwork for the same sort of election challenges that occurred before a mob of his supporters stormed the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021.

“We are not doing anything improper. We’re not doing anything we’re not allowed to do. And we have to let the process play out," Blanche said. "But I do think it’s important for the American people to understand that we are not — (and) President Trump is not — trying to take over a state election in any way shape or form.”
The lawsuit, he told CBS' “Face the Nation,” is meant to “put guardrails in place” to preserve possible evidence of voter confusion at the polls.

“It’s not saying, ‘Don’t certify.’ It’s saying, ‘If a court ultimately determines that it was decided because of confusion and not the will of the voters, then we do not think the states should certify.’ And that’s consistent with federal law and consistent with even Alaskan law, if that happens,” he said.
Associated Press writer Josh Boak contributed to this report.

华盛顿 - 华盛顿（美联社） - 周日，司法部长托德·布兰奇为特朗普政府提起的诉讼进行了辩护，该诉讼旨在阻止共和党现任议员丹·沙利文输掉阿拉斯加州参议院选举结果，并认为法律挑战是避免在备受关注的中期选举中让选民感到困惑的必要步骤。
布兰奇对 ​​CNN 的《国情咨文》节目表示，唐纳德·特朗普总统周五表示，他是“那个说要做就做的人”，他并没有试图在 11 月 3 日大选的风口浪尖上“以任何方式、形式”推翻州选举结果。
“我们希望我们不必这样做。我们希望能有一个有效的解决方案，”布兰奇说。
共和党人担心，选票上的第二位候选人丹·沙利文（Dan Sullivan）是一位来自彼得堡小渔村的退休教师和学校管理人员，他可能会从参议员那里夺走选票，并使选举结果有利于民主党人、前国会女议员玛丽·佩尔托拉（Mary Peltola）。
周四提起诉讼的第二天，佩尔托拉称其“在我看来是公然、公然的腐败”，也是共和党人的转移注意力的策略。阿拉斯加的另一位共和党参议员丽莎·默科斯基也在社交媒体帖子中批评了这起诉讼。
特朗普周日告诉记者，他认为这次投票是非法的，因为它不公平，并且应该向选民表明参议员沙利文是现任参议员。
“至少让他使用参议员丹·沙利文（Dan Sullivan）的名字，而不是现任参议员的名字，因为很多人不知道现任参议员的含义，”特朗普说。
阿拉斯加选民将在选票上看到“丹·S·沙利文”被标识为“注册共和党”和“现任”，而“小丹尼尔·J·沙利文”则被标识为“注册共和党”和“现任”。不会有党派关系。
在共和党总统任命布兰奇领导司法部之前，布兰奇作为特朗普的私人律师代表特朗普，司法部在阿拉斯加提起了诉讼。在选民选举特朗普连任白宫之前，布兰奇在选举推论案中为特朗普辩护，有效结束了刑事起诉。
特朗普告诉司法部，如果共和党以微弱优势落败，将提起诉讼以阻止阿拉斯加州参议院的结果

布兰奇告诉 CNN 主持人达纳·巴什 (Dana Bash)，她问他特朗普是否试图为 2021 年 1 月 6 日他的支持者暴徒冲进美国国会大厦之前发生的同样类型的选举挑战奠定基础，这太“疯狂”了。
“我们没有做任何不当的事情。我们没有做任何不被允许做的事情。我们必须让这个过程顺利进行，”布兰奇说。 “但我确实认为，美国人民必须明白，我们不会——（而且）特朗普总统也不会——试图以任何方式接管州选举。”
他告诉哥伦比亚广播公司的“面对全国”节目，该诉讼旨在“设置护栏”，以保留选民在投票时感到困惑的可能证据。
“这并不是说，‘不要认证’。而是说，‘如果法院最终认定该决定是由于混乱而不是选民的意愿而做出的，那么我们认为各州不应该认证。’这符合联邦法律，如果发生这种情况，甚至也符合阿拉斯加的法律，”他说。

body_en: President Trump's Board of Peace has appointed Shelley Greenspan, who served as the White House's Jewish community liaison during the Biden administration, to lead its outreach to Congress and the Washington think tank community.

Why it matters: Greenspan's selection is part of an effort by the Board of Peace to increase bipartisan support for President Trump's Gaza peace plan. The implementation of the plan is expected to get a renewed push after the midterms and the formation of a new Israeli government.
The possibility of Democrats controlling the House or Senate makes the need for bipartisanship on the Gaza plan even more crucial.
Driving the news: The plan has been stuck due to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's refusal to take any steps in Gaza before the October 27 elections.
In recent months, multiple prominent Democrats have expressed support for Trump's plan. Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton endorsed the plan in June, calling it the most viable proposal.

Zoom in: Greenspan, a career civil servant at the State Department, was at the White House National Security Council during Biden's term — both as the American Jewish community liaison and the director for partnerships and elobal engagement.
At the Board of Peace she will lead external affairs, putting her in charge of outreach to Congress and Middle East experts.

What they're saying: "Shelley brings deep experience working across the aisle, having earned the trust of Democrats and Republicans alike through her service at the White House, National Security Council, and State Department in Democratic and Republican administrations," the Board of Peace told Axios in a statement.
"Sustained, bipartisan support from Congress is essential to the work ahead, and Shelley is uniquely capable of leading this effort," the board added.
Greenspan told Axios in a statement that she worked in her last State Department role to advance Trump's "vision for peace and prosperity in the Middle East."
"I saw how the President's 20-Point Plan can tangibly deliver for the peoples of Gaza and Israel. I look forward to continuing that work with the Board," she said.

为什么重要：格林斯潘的选择是和平委员会为增加两党对特朗普总统加沙和平计划的支持而做出的努力的一部分。预计该计划的实施将在中期选举和以色列新政府组建后得到新的推动。
民主党控制众议院或参议院的可能性使得加沙计划上两党合作的必要性变得更加重要。
最新消息：由于以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡拒绝在 10 月 27 日选举之前在加沙采取任何措施，该计划陷入停滞。

在和平委员会，她将领导对外事务，负责与国会和中东专家的联系。
他们的说法：和平委员会在一份声明中告诉 Axios，“雪莱带来了跨党派工作的丰富经验，通过她在白宫、国家安全委员会以及国务院在民主党和共和党政府中的服务，赢得了民主党和共和党的信任。”
董事会补充说：“国会的持续、两党支持对于未来的工作至关重要，而雪莱具有领导这项工作的独特能力。”
格林斯潘在一份声明中告诉 Axios，她在国务院的最后一个职务是为了推进特朗普的“中东和平与繁荣愿景”。
“我看到了总统的 20 点计划如何切实为加沙和以色列人民带来好处。我期待着与委员会继续开展这项工作，”她说。

summary: Suit that cites 2025 Guardian investigation alleges ‘pattern of inaccurate pricing’ that ‘affects millions of purchases’ The Federal Trade Commission and 20 states have sued Dollar General, the nation’s largest dollar-store chain, for persistently overcharging

body_en: FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General, accusing bargain chain of overcharging customers | US news
FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General, accusing bargain chain of overcharging customers
Suit that cites 2025 Guardian investigation alleges ‘pattern of inaccurate pricing’ that ‘affects millions of purchases’

The Federal Trade Commission and 20 states have sued Dollar General, the nation’s largest dollar-store chain, for persistently overcharging customers at its more than 20,000 stores across the United States.
The lawsuit , filed in federal court in Nashville, cites a Guardian investigation published last December.
“Dollar General has for years engaged in deceptive conduct that harms the very consumers it claims to serve,” said the 95-page legal complaint.

“Although Dollar General promises convenience, low prices, and value, the company has routinely charged customers more at the register than the prices displayed on shelves, price tags, and advertisements. This pattern of inaccurate pricing has persisted for years and affects millions of purchases across the country.”
How the dollar-store industry overcharges cash-strapped customers while promising low prices
The lawsuit says the scope of the retail chain’s “pricing misconduct” is “staggering”.

The FTC is the federal agency charged with protecting consumers from deceptive, unfair and anticompetitive business practices. State authorities from Mississippi to Ohio to Nebraska to Utah have joined the case as plaintiffs.
Dollar General did not respond to questions for this story, but has previously said that it was “committed to providing customers with accurate prices on items purchased in our stores”.

The FTC’s allegations are consistent with the Guardian’s December 2025 investigation , which found that Dollar General stores failed more than 4,300 government price-accuracy inspections in 23 states over a three-year period. That article “was the subject of significant internal deliberation and discussions” within the company, the lawsuit said.

The agency noted in the lawsuit that Dollar General has policies in place that are supposed to align register prices with shelf prices. For example, it directs employees to remove and replace outdated labels on certain days of the week. Workers told the Guardian that, because of understaffing, they are often too busy to change those labels.
“Dollar General’s on-paper policies to update pricing achieve little in practice,” the lawsuit said, because “they do not track whether the printed labels are actually affixed to shelves.”
The FTC cited a Guardian interview with a lead sales associate in Louisiana who said: “I threw away tags sometimes, to keep me or a co-worker out of trouble.”

Dollar General told the Guardian in 2025 that it is “disappointed” any time it fails to deliver on its commitment to accurate shelf pricing. In court documents in Ohio, Dollar General’s lawyers have argued that “it is virtually impossible for a retailer to match shelf pricing and scanned pricing 100% of the time for all items. Perfection in this regard is neither plausible nor expected under the law.”

In a statement accompanying the FTC lawsuit, the federal agency noted that Dollar General markets itself as a low-cost alternative to other retailers, and that low- and fixed-income customers rely on the accuracy of its price labels.

“Dollar General has betrayed the trust of millions of American consumers and imposed significant financial harm on communities and consumers who are already struggling to make their paychecks last,” said Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC’s bureau of consumer protection.

In a separate case, the New York attorney general, Letitia James, announced earlier this month that Dollar General had agreed to a $1.875m deal to settle allegations that it had repeatedly overcharged customers across the state.

诉讼援引 2025 年卫报调查称“定价不准确的模式”“影响了数百万次购买”
美国联邦贸易委员会和 20 个州已起诉美国最大的一元店连锁店 Dollar General，称其在全美 20,000 多家门店持续向顾客收取过高费用。
该诉讼向纳什维尔联邦法院提起，引用了去年 12 月发表的《卫报》调查结果。
这份长达 95 页的法律诉状称，“Dollar General 多年来一直从事欺骗行为，损害了其声称服务的消费者。”
“尽管 Dollar General 承诺提供便利、价格低廉和物有所值，但该公司在收银台向顾客收取的费用通常高于货架、价格标签和广告上显示的价格。这种不准确定价的模式已经持续多年，影响了全国数以百万计的购买行为。”
一元店行业如何向现金短缺的顾客收取过高费用，同时又承诺低价
该诉讼称，该零售连锁店“定价不当行为”的范围“令人震惊”。
FTC 是负责保护消费者免受欺骗、不公平和反竞争商业行为侵害的联邦机构。从密西西比州到俄亥俄州，从内布拉斯加州到犹他州，各州当局都作为原告加入了此案。
Dollar General 没有回应本文的问题，但此前曾表示，它“致力于为顾客提供在我们商店购买的商品的准确价格”。
FTC 的指控与《卫报》2025 年 12 月的调查一致，该调查发现 Dollar General 商店在三年内未通过 23 个州的 4,300 多次政府价格准确性检查。诉讼称，这篇文章是公司内部“重大内部审议和讨论的主题”。
该机构在诉讼中指出，Dollar General 制定了旨在使注册价格与货架价格保持一致的政策。例如，它指示员工在一周的某些日子删除和更换过时的标签。工人们告诉卫报，由于人手不足，他们往往太忙而无暇更换这些标签。
诉讼称，“Dollar General 更新定价的纸质政策在实践中收效甚微，”​​因为“他们没有追踪印刷标签是否确实贴在货架上。”
联邦贸易委员会援引《卫报》对路易斯安那州一位首席销售助理的采访，他说：“我有时会扔掉标签，以免我或同事遇到麻烦。”
Dollar General 在 2025 年向《卫报》表示，只要它未能兑现准确货架定价的承诺，它就会“感到失望”。在俄亥俄州的法庭文件中，Dollar General 的律师辩称，“零售商实际上不可能对所有商品 100% 匹配货架定价和扫描定价。根据法律，这方面的完美既不合理，也不期望实现。”
在联邦贸易委员会诉讼附带的一份声明中，该联邦机构指出，Dollar General 将自己定位为其他零售商的低成本替代品，低收入和固定收入客户依赖其价格标签的准确性。
美国联邦贸易委员会消费者保护局局长克里斯托弗·穆法里奇 (Christopher Mufarrige) 表示：“Dollar General 背叛了数百万美国消费者的信任，给已经在为维持工资而苦苦挣扎的社区和消费者造成了重大经济损失。”
在另一起案件中，纽约州总检察长利蒂西亚·詹姆斯 (Letitia James) 本月早些时候宣布，Dollar General 已同意达成 187.5 万美元的协议，以和解对其多次向全州客户收取过高费用的指控。

Editor's Note: Late Monday, in a blow to the administration, the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals denied the Department of Justice’s request to block California from counting some 20,000 mail-in ballots from voters it alleges are potential non-citizens.

It's crunch time for candidates across the country with Election Day just over a week away. On Monday, President Trump campaigned in ruby-red Mississippi, a state he won by almost 23 points two years ago. Over the weekend, the battleground state of Michigan saw a political heavyweight bout between Trump and former President Obama. Liz Landers reports.

It is crunch time for candidates across the country, as tomorrow marks exactly one week from Election Day. President Trump is spending today campaigning in ruby-red Mississippi, a state he won by almost 23 points two years ago. And it was the battleground state of Michigan that saw a political heavyweight bout this weekend between Mr. Trump and former President Barack Obama.
Stumping in swing states this weekend, President Trump laid out what's at stake in the looming midterm elections now just eight days away.

In the tight Michigan race that will help decide control of the Senate between former Republican Congressman Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, the president attacked El-Sayed's faith and said he would be a threat to national security.

I'm here to keep a jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator. And that's the fact. We're not going to let that happen. The people of Michigan are going to defeat Abdul Mohamed Sayed.
I don't care how he pronounces my name. I don't even care that he remembers my whole name, because he can just go on and call me senator after November.
El-Sayed, who would be the nation's first Muslim Senator, said Trump's attacks were a distraction from voters' concerns about the economy.

In a contentious interview on NBC's "Meet the Press," El-Sayed's opponent, Mike Rogers, dug in on his allegations linking El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood, even though there is no evidence that El-Sayed has any affiliation with the group.

No, I don't. I have never called him a terrorist. I have never called him a terrorist. This election is about me versus Abdul. I mean, he's a Democrat Socialists of America-aligned candidate who has these pretty radical support groups that don't like America.

Former President Barack Obama brought his own firepower to the trail, rallying Democratic voters in two Midwestern battlegrounds on Saturday, telling crowds in Michigan and Ohio that Trump was responsible for rising costs because of the war with Iran.
The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions.
Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody has for -- nobody voted for.
And as President Trump has made many mentions of his Washington, D.C., renovation projects while on the trail, the former president mocked that preoccupation.
What's up with the gold? Everything more gold. He's got the white ass looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.
Voters who waited in line for Mr. Trump and Mr. Obama's rallies this weekend spoke about what will draw them to the polls.
Why am I here? I'm here for the future of this country, because I know we're at a crossroads.

对于全国候选人来说，现在是关键时刻，因为明天距离选举日正好一周。特朗普总统今天在宝石红色的密西西比州进行竞选活动，两年前他以近 23 个百分点的优势赢得了该州。本周末，特朗普和前总统巴拉克·奥巴马在战场州密歇根州进行了一场重量级政治较量。

我不在乎他如何发音我的名字。我什至不在乎他是否记得我的全名，因为他可以在十一月之后继续称呼我为参议员。

由于特朗普总统在旅途中多次提到他的华盛顿特区改造项目，这位前总统嘲笑了这种专注。
黄金怎么了？一切都更加黄金。他的屁股很白，看起来就像萨达姆·侯赛因开了一家芝士蛋糕工厂。

Massachusetts lesbian bar makes frantic effort to find new owners after relaxing masking policy
Last Ditch bar announced it would ‘soft close’ after it went viral following a story on its attempt to relax Covid rules
A Massachusetts lesbian bar that went viral for loosening its Covid mask policy last month announced plans to “soft close” on Monday as it seeks new ownership.

The Last Ditch bar, in the small city of Greenfield, said in an Instagram post that it was searching for co-owners, new owners or a full sale, and that it would “soft close effective immediately”, with “only booked events” continuing while it closes this winter. It had opened just last year as a bar for “dykes, transsexuals, gender freaks, workers, and their friends”.

Last month the bar went viral following a Boston Globe story documenting a masking dispute after the owners attempted to relax the bar’s Covid mask-wearing policy for one night a week in a bid to drive up Saturday business. The bar had been struggling to raise revenue while adhering to a strict policy of mask-wearing, but the proposed change prompted a backlash from customers who accused the owners of ableism and abandoning immunocompromised people.
There was then a backlash to those critics, with people piling on and mocking customers’ concerns about contracting Covid.

The publicity did also attract some support to the bar, but evidently, not enough. “We put our lives on hold to foster networks of care, resources and a home base for organizing. It’s time we pass it on,” the bar said on Instagram.

“We’ve been fighting since the beginning to fill out the team, and we still don’t have a board/leadership to manage workers’ owned co-op transfer. We are soft closing effective immediately; all booked events will continue; otherwise, we are closed.”
In seeking new ownership, the bar noted that the sale would include the furniture, equipment, inventory and social media pages, to an estimated value of $70,000.

As set out in the Globe’s article, the bar was already in financial trouble before the masking furor, and two of the three original owners had dropped out of the project. The remaining owner was left with the responsibility of repaying the $50,000 loan the three took out to open the bar and was living out of her truck and working several jobs to try to keep it running.
The Guardian has reached out to the Last Ditch bar for comment.
