马萨诸塞州女同性恋酒吧在放宽遮盖政策后疯狂寻找新主人
Last Ditch 酒吧因试图放宽新冠疫情规定而被疯传，随后宣布将“软关闭”
马萨诸塞州一家女同性恋酒吧上个月因放松新冠口罩政策而走红，该酒吧宣布计划在周一“软关闭”，以寻求新的所有权。
位于小城市格林菲尔德的 Last Ditch 酒吧在 Instagram 上发帖称，正在寻找共同业主、新业主或全面出售，并将“立即软关闭”，在今年冬天关闭期间，“仅预订活动”将继续进行。它于去年刚刚开业，是一家为“堤坝、变性人、性别怪胎、工人和他们的朋友”服务的酒吧。
上个月，《波士顿环球报》的一篇报道记录了一场戴口罩的纠纷，酒吧老板试图放宽酒吧每周一晚佩戴新冠口罩的政策，以提高周六的营业额，这使得该酒吧迅速走红。该酒吧一直在努力提高收入，同时坚持严格的戴口罩政策，但拟议的改变引起了顾客的强烈反对，他们指责酒吧老板存在体能歧视，并抛弃了免疫功能低下的人。
随后，这些批评者遭到了强烈反对，人们纷纷嘲笑顾客对感染新冠病毒的担忧。
这种宣传确实也为酒吧赢得了一些支持，但显然还不够。 “我们把自己的生活搁置起来，以培育护理网络、资源和组织基地。现在是我们传承下去的时候了，”酒吧在 Instagram 上表示。
“我们从一开始就一直在努力充实团队，但我们仍然没有董事会/领导层来管理工人拥有的合作社转让。我们的软关闭立即生效；所有预订的活动将继续；否则，我们将关闭。”
在寻求新的所有权时，该酒吧指出，此次出售将包括家具、设备、库存和社交媒体页面，估计价值 70,000 美元。
正如《环球报》的文章所述，在掩盖风波之前，酒吧就已经陷入财务困境，三名原业主中的两人已经退出了该项目。剩下的老板有责任偿还三人为开设酒吧而借的 50,000 美元贷款，她住在她的卡车里，并打几份工作以维持其运转。
《卫报》已联系 Last Ditch 酒吧征求意见。

title_en: Trump escalates anti-Muslim attacks against El-Sayed in Michigan
title_zh: 特朗普在密歇根州升级了针对埃尔赛义德的反穆斯林攻击
summary: President Trump intensified his anti-Muslim rhetoric against Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday, portraying him as a threat to national security and questioning his loyalty to the United States.
summary_zh: 周日，特朗普总统强化了针对密歇根州参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的反穆斯林言论，将他描绘成对国家的威胁。
body_en: Trump escalates anti-Muslim attacks against El-Sayed in Michigan

President Donald Trump departs after speaking during a campaign rally at McMorran Place Sports and Entertainment Center, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026, in Port Huron, Mich. Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP hide caption

PORT HURON, Mich. — President Donald Trump intensified his anti-Muslim rhetoric against Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday, portraying him as a threat to national security and questioning his loyalty to the United States in remarks that drew a sharp rebuke from a former top Arab American ally.
Republicans are spending millions and still may not win districts drawn to favor them

Trump called El-Sayed, a former Detroit health official, a "jihadist" who was "on the side of the terrorists" and would "have to go through a metal detector before he's allowed to go into the Senate." He also repeatedly invoked the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, drawing a comparison between stopping El-Sayed from entering the Senate chamber and the passengers who fought back against the hijackers aboard United Flight 93.

El-Sayed, who would become the nation's first Muslim senator if elected, has called attacks on his loyalty to the country "shameful" and repeatedly denied any ties to extremist groups. The Republican president's remarks were condemned by Bishara Bahbah, a founder of Arab Americans for Trump, the group that helped lead the president's outreach to Arab American voters in 2024.
"The president's statements are out of line," he said in a phone interview. "They are crossing a red line. They are racist."

With Republicans on the defensive over inflation, soaring fuel prices and the Iran war, the president has been trying to generate turnout by claiming that El-Sayed and other Democrats are existential threats to America, instead of electoral rivals. Michigan's Senate race between El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers is among a handful of contests that could determine control of the chamber.

Trump made his remarks in Port Huron, a Canadian border city about an hour north of Detroit and near communities where he made significant gains among Arab American voters in 2024. He became the first Republican presidential candidate since 2000 to win Dearborn, a city with one of the nation's largest concentrations of Arab Americans.

Trump, who imposed a travel ban targeting several predominantly Muslim countries during his first term, has increasingly leaned into anti-Muslim rhetoric as Election Day approaches. He also attacked Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota at Sunday's rally, where he declared that he had come to Michigan "to keep a jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator."
Responding to Trump, who also regularly mocks his name, El-Sayed told supporters at a rally in Grand Rapids later Sunday that he doesn't care how Trump pronounces or misrepresents it.
"I don't even care that he remembers my whole name because he can just go on and call me 'senator' after November," El-Sayed said, drawing cheers. "I will be Senator Muhammad to you, bro."
El-Sayed's faith, associations and past statements become campaign flashpoints

Central to Republicans' strategy against El-Sayed in the final weeks of the campaign has been an effort to link him to the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamic movement with branches that the U.S. government has designated as terrorist organizations.

There is no evidence that El-Sayed has any affiliation with the Muslim Brotherhood. His half-sister, Eman Abdelhadi, wrote on social media in 2012 that "my family has long been MB" and described a conversation with her mother about her involvement in the Muslim Brotherhood in the early 1970s.
El-Sayed was born in the United States to Egyptian immigrant parents who divorced when he was young. He was raised by his father, not his biological mother.
Polls are a snapshot, and other helpful things to remember during the midterm elections
Trump on Sunday also targeted El-Sayed's ties to popular streamer Hasan Piker, who appeared alongside the Democrat multiple times during the primary campaign, including at his election night event.
Piker in the past has said that "Hamas is a thousand times better" than Israel, describing some Orthodox Jews as "inbred" and that "America deserved 9/11."

El-Sayed has faced criticism for his own rhetoric. He has repeatedly refused to answer questions about whether Iran or Israel poses a bigger threat to the country. Earlier this year, he said "hurt people hurt people" after an attack on a synagogue in the Detroit area. The attacker had lost four relatives in an Israeli airstrike on Lebanon the week earlier. El-Sayed later apologized, saying he was not trying to justify what happened.
body_zh: 特朗普在密歇根州升级了针对埃尔赛义德的反穆斯林攻击
2026 年 10 月 25 日星期日，唐纳德·特朗普总统在密歇根州休伦港麦克莫兰广场体育和娱乐中心举行的竞选集会上发表讲话后离开。朱莉娅·德马里·尼欣森/美联社隐藏标题栏
密歇根州休伦港——周日，唐纳德·特朗普总统强化了针对密歇根州参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的反穆斯林言论，将他描绘成对国家安全的威胁，并质疑他对美国的忠诚度，其言论遭到了一位前阿拉伯裔美国盟友的严厉谴责。
共和党花费了数百万美元，但仍然可能无法赢得支持他们的选区
特朗普称前底特律卫生官员埃尔赛义德是“圣战分子”，“站在恐怖分子一边”，“在获准进入参议院之前必须通过金属探测器”。他还多次援引2001年9月11日的恐怖袭击事件，将阻止埃尔赛义德进入参议院会议厅与联合航空93号航班上的劫机者进行反击的乘客进行比较。
如果当选，埃尔赛义德将成为该国第一位穆斯林参议员，他称针对他对国家忠诚的攻击是“可耻的”，并一再否认与极端主义团体有任何联系。这位共和党总统的言论遭到了特朗普阿拉伯裔美国人组织创始人比沙拉·巴巴(Bishara Bahbah)的谴责，该组织帮助领导总统在2024年向阿拉伯裔美国选民进行宣传。
“总统的言论不合时宜，”他在电话采访中说。 “他们正在跨越红线。他们是种族主义者。”
由于共和党在通货膨胀、燃油价格飙升和伊朗战争等问题上处于守势，总统一直试图通过声称埃尔赛义德和其他民主党人对美国的生存构成威胁，而不是选举竞争对手来提高投票率。埃尔-赛义德和共和党人迈克·罗杰斯之间的密歇根州参议院竞选是可能决定参议院控制权的少数竞争之一。
特朗普在加拿大边境城市休伦港发表讲话，该城市距离底特律以北约一小时车程，靠近社区，2024 年他在阿拉伯裔美国选民中获得了显着的支持。他成为 2000 年以来第一位赢得迪尔伯恩的共和党总统候选人，迪尔伯恩是美国阿拉伯裔美国人最集中的城市之一。
特朗普在第一个任期内对几个以穆斯林为主的国家实施了旅行禁令，随着选举日的临近，他越来越倾向于反穆斯林言论。他还在周日的集会上攻击了明尼苏达州的民主党众议员伊尔汗·奥马尔，他在会上宣称自己来到密歇根州“是为了阻止圣战穆斯林兄弟会成员成为美国参议员”。
周日晚些时候，埃尔-赛义德在大急流城的一次集会上对支持者们说，他不在乎特朗普如何发音或歪曲它，以回应特朗普也经常嘲笑他的名字。
“我什至不在乎他是否记得我的全名，因为十一月之后他就可以继续叫我‘参议员’，”埃尔-赛义德说道，引来欢呼声。 “我将成为你的参议员穆罕默德，兄弟。”
埃尔-赛义德的信仰、关联和过去的言论成为竞选热点
共和党在竞选最后几周针对埃尔赛义德的战略核心是努力将他与穆斯林兄弟会联系起来，穆斯林兄弟会是一个伊斯兰运动，其分支已被美国政府指定为恐怖组织。
没有证据表明赛义德与穆斯林兄弟会有任何关系。他同父异母的妹妹伊曼·阿卜杜勒哈迪 (Eman Abdelhadi) 2012 年在社交媒体上写道，“我的家人长期以来一直是 MB”，并描述了与她母亲关于她在 20 世纪 70 年代初参与穆斯林兄弟会的对话。
埃尔-赛义德出生于美国，父母是埃及移民，他们在他年轻时就离婚了。他是由他的父亲抚养长大的，而不是他的亲生母亲。
民意调查只是一个快照，以及中期选举期间需要记住的其他有用的事情
特朗普周日还针对埃尔-赛义德与受欢迎的流媒体哈桑·皮克的关系，后者在初选期间多次与民主党一起出现，包括在他的选举之夜活动中。
皮克过去曾说过，“哈马斯比以色列强一千倍”，并将一些正统犹太人描述为“近亲繁殖”，并称“9/11是美国应得的”。
埃尔-赛义德因其言论而受到批评。他一再拒绝回答有关伊朗或以色列是否对该国构成更大威胁的问题。今年早些时候，他在底特律地区一座犹太教堂遭到袭击后表示，“受伤的人受伤了”。袭击者在一周前以色列对黎巴嫩的空袭中失去了四名亲属。埃尔-赛义德后来道歉，称他并不是想为所发生的事情辩护。

title_en: Coastal California braces for flooding amid forecast of ‘record-breaking tides’
title_zh: 加州沿海地区预计将出现“破纪录的潮汐”，应对洪水
summary: Residents of coastal towns told to avoid beaches during high tides and keep further away from the ocean than usual Coastal communities across California were preparing for days of flooding amid potentially “record-breaking tides” this week, as water levels beg
summary_zh: 沿海城镇的居民被告知在涨潮期间避开海滩，并比平时远离海洋 加州各地的沿海社区
body_en: Coastal California braces for flooding amid forecast of ‘record-breaking tides’ | California
Coastal California braces for flooding amid forecast of ‘record-breaking tides’
Residents of coastal towns told to avoid beaches during high tides and keep further away from the ocean than usual
Coastal communities across California were preparing for days of flooding amid potentially “record-breaking tides” this week, as water levels began rising on Monday.

The National Weather Service warned that significant coastal flooding was expected in San Diego and Orange counties through Thursday that could close roads and inundate homes, businesses and critical infrastructure. A wide swath of the coast from San Luis Obispo county to Los Angeles county could see “minor to moderate” coastal flooding with tides as high as 8ft. Further north in the Bay Area, officials advised there could be as much as 2.1ft of inundation, primarily in low-lying coastal areas.
The effects could be seen in the Marin county community of Mill Valley where footage captured cars stuck on a flooded road, as paddleboarders moved past.

By Monday morning, the NWS office in Los Angeles reported that it was already seeing record tides. Preliminary observations from the agency’s San Pedro tide gauge were at 8.02ft, the highest seen in data dating back to November 1923.

“Avoid the beaches during high tides, keep farther back from the ocean than usual (waves will run much farther up the beach that expected), stay off rock walls/jetties, and make sure flood-prone property is protected this week,” the NWS office in San Diego said in a statement.

More than a week before the exceptionally high tides were forecast to arrive, the Orange county city of Newport Beach declared a local emergency to prepare for flooding. Staff were deploying across the area to inspect infrastructure, reinforce beach berms and install sandbags and other equipment, the city said. Newport Beach is providing free sandbags and advised residents to inspect vulnerable areas around their properties.
Due to El Niño and the Kelvin wave , ocean water levels in the region have already been about 15 to 22in higher than expected, the Newport Beach city manager, Seimone Jurjis, said in a statement .

“A foot and a half may not sound like much, but in a coastal community like ours, it can mean the difference between water staying below a seawall and water spilling into streets, garages and homes, especially during some of the highest tides of the year,” Jurjis said.

This month has already brought extreme weather in the region, including flooding that overtook city streets and large waves that struck beachside homes. The remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel left a trail of destruction in California, significantly damaging homes, destroying a boardwalk and forcing residents to evacuate.
With a historic El Niño unfolding in the Pacific, California is expected to face severe storms this winter.
body_zh: 预测“破纪录的潮汐”，加州沿海地区将面临洪水加利福尼亚州
加州沿海地区预计将出现“破纪录的潮汐”，应对洪水
沿海城镇的居民被告知在涨潮期间避开海滩，并比平时远离海洋
随着水位从周一开始上升，加州各地的沿海社区正在为本周可能出现的“破纪录的潮汐”中的数日洪水做好准备。
美国国家气象局警告称，预计周四圣地亚哥和奥兰治县将出现严重沿海洪水，道路可能关闭，房屋、企业和关键基础设施可能被淹没。从圣路易斯奥比斯波县到洛杉矶县的大片海岸可能会出现“轻微到中度”的沿海洪水，潮汐高达 8 英尺。官员们表示，在湾区更北的地区，洪水可能高达 2.1 英尺，主要发生在低洼的沿海地区。
在米尔谷的马林县社区可以看到这种影响，那里的镜头捕捉到了当桨板冲浪者经过时，汽车被困在被洪水淹没的道路上。
到周一早上，美国国家气象局驻洛杉矶办事处报告说，已经出现创纪录的潮汐。该机构圣佩德罗验潮仪的初步观测结果为 8.02 英尺，是 1923 年 11 月以来数据中的最高值。
国家气象局圣地亚哥办事处在一份声明中表示：“在涨潮期间避开海滩，比平时远离海洋（海浪会比预期的更远地冲上海滩），远离岩壁/码头，并确保本周容易发生洪水的财产受到保护。”
在预计异常高潮到来的一个多星期前，奥兰治县纽波特比奇市宣布当地进入紧急状态，为洪水做好准备。该市表示，工作人员正在该地区部署检查基础设施、加固海滩护堤并安装沙袋和其他设备。纽波特海滩正在提供免费沙袋，并建议居民检查其房产周围的脆弱区域。
纽波特比奇城市经理 Seimone Jurjis 在一份声明中表示，由于厄尔尼诺现象和开尔文波，该地区的海水水位已经比预期高出约 15 至 22 英寸。
“一英尺半听起来似乎不多，但在像我们这样的沿海社区，这可能意味着海堤以下的水和溢出到街道、车库和房屋的水之间的区别，特别是在一年中的一些最高潮汐期间，”尤吉斯说。
本月该地区已经出现了极端天气，包括淹没城市街道的洪水和袭击海滨房屋的巨浪。热带风暴雷切尔的残余物在加利福尼亚州留下了严重的破坏痕迹，严重破坏了房屋，摧毁了木板路并迫使居民撤离。
随着历史性的厄尔尼诺现象在太平洋上发生，加州预计今年冬天将面临严重的风暴。

title_en: Trump offers $1 million reward for voter fraud tips that lead to convictions
title_zh: 特朗普悬赏100万美元奖励那些导致定罪的选民欺诈举报
summary: It’s unclear where the money would come from for Trump’s latest effort to crack down on purported voter fraud ahead of the midterm elections.
summary_zh: 目前尚不清楚特朗普在中期选举前打击所谓的选民欺诈行为的最新举措的资金将从何而来。
body_en: Trump offers $1 million reward for voter fraud tips that lead to convictions
President Donald Trump said Monday that he is offering $1 million to anyone who reports voter fraud in the upcoming election or past ones.

Trump did not specify where the funds for such payments would come from. He said on Truth Social that they would be paid on the “arrest and conviction of those that created the fraud.” A White House spokesperson did not offer more details about the offer, referring NBC News to Trump’s post.
There is no evidence of widespread voter fraud in U.S. elections, though Trump has spent years claiming that there is and that it cost him the 2020 election he lost.

Instances of voter fraud do occur on occasion — such as when people fill out recently deceased relatives’ ballots or lie on mail ballot applications — and they are usually caught. A tracker from the conservative Heritage Foundation has collected more than 1,600 incidents of voter fraud over 40 years, a tiny fraction of the total votes cast over that period.

Trump’s offer Monday is his latest effort to exert greater influence over the midterm elections. His administration has dedicated significant resources to searching for noncitizens on states’ voter rolls. The Justice Department sued California officials in an attempt to force them to segregate mail ballots it says went to potential noncitizens. Noncitizen voting is also rare , studies show.
Last week, the Justice Department sued Alaska officials , at Trump’s request, to prevent the results of the U.S. Senate race from being certified if GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan loses.
Courts have also blocked Trump from making sweeping changes to mail voting and requiring documentary proof of citizenship to vote.
Trump’s voter fraud reward announcement comes after he unveiled a $25 million government fraud whistleblower program, telling reporters he’d decide who was worthy of the prize .

He has also been making other financial promises as he hits the campaign trail for Republicans ahead of the midterms, including $5,000 payments to Americans if his party maintains control of Congress. Trump has similarly not clarified where the money for those payments would come from.
Jane C. Timm is a senior reporter for NBC News.
body_zh: 特朗普悬赏100万美元奖励那些导致定罪的选民欺诈举报
唐纳德·特朗普总统周一表示，他将向举报即将到来的选举或过去选举中选民欺诈行为的任何人提供 100 万美元。
特朗普没有具体说明此类付款的资金将来自哪里。他在《Truth Social》节目中表示，如果“逮捕并定罪制造欺诈的人”，他们将获得报酬。白宫发言人没有提供有关该提议的更多细节，而是向 NBC 新闻提及了特朗普的帖子。
没有证据表明美国选举中存在广泛的选民欺诈行为，尽管特朗普多年来一直声称存在这种情况，并且这让他在 2020 年选举中失利。
选民欺诈的情况确实偶尔会发生，例如当人们填写最近去世的亲属的选票或在邮寄选票申请表上撒谎时，他们通常会被抓住。保守派传统基金会的追踪者收集了 40 年来 1,600 多起选民舞弊事件，仅占该时期总投票数的一小部分。
特朗普周一的提议是他对中期选举施加更大影响的最新努力。他的政府投入了大量资源来寻找各州选民名册上的非公民。司法部起诉加州官员，试图迫使他们将邮寄选票分开，据称这些选票发给了潜在的非公民。研究表明，非公民投票也很少见。
上周，司法部应特朗普的要求起诉阿拉斯加官员，以阻止共和党参议员丹·沙利文输掉美国参议院竞选结果。
法院还阻止特朗普对邮寄投票进行彻底改变，并要求提供公民身份证明文件才能投票。
特朗普宣布选民欺诈奖励之前，他公布了一项价值 2500 万美元的政府欺诈举报计划，并告诉记者，他将决定谁有资格获得该奖项。
在中期选举前为共和党竞选时，他还做出了其他财务承诺，其中包括如果共和党继续控制国会，将向美国人支付 5,000 美元。特朗普同样没有澄清这些付款的资金将来自哪里。
Jane C. Timm 是 NBC 新闻的高级记者。

title_en: Spurned by Trump, these outgoing Republicans aren’t helping their potential successors
title_zh: 被特朗普抛弃的这些即将离任的共和党人并没有帮助他们的潜在继任者
summary: They were snubbed on their way out of office. Their revenge is indifference.
summary_zh: 他们在卸任时遭到冷落。他们的报复是冷漠。
body_en: Republicans spurned by President Donald Trump aren't interested in rescuing their would-be replacements.
Instead, a growing number of retiring or ousted GOP incumbents from Nevada to North Carolina are sitting those races out, and in some cases, openly bucking their own party.

Outgoing Sen. John Cornyn has raised money for various Republican Senate candidates — just not for Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who ousted him in the primary with support from Trump. He’s been vocal for months about what he sees as Paxton’s vulnerabilities and how Democrats could flip Texas blue for the first time in decades.

North Carolina Sen. Thom Tillis — who has frequently criticized some of Trump’s Cabinet and broken with the White House on policy — has played little role in the campaign of former RNC Chair Michael Whatley, Trump’s hand-picked Senate candidate. The distance between the two Republicans is particularly notable as Whatley struggles to close the gap against Democrat Roy Cooper.
Rep. Mark Amodei has repeatedly criticized, and now openly rejected voting for , the GOP nominee to replace him, David Flippo.

“The bedwetting from outgoing moderate Republicans will define their legacy and only help socialists get elected,” said David McIntosh, president of the Trump-aligned Club for Growth, which has endorsed Flippo and Paxton. “People like John Cornyn and Mark Amodei need to get on board and support Republican nominees and stop posturing for an MSNOW contract.”

But other Republicans defended their colleagues: “I never would question the loyalty to the party of Thom Tillis or John Cornyn. Both of them have contributed immensely to our party and our party's successes in the past and I suspect will be going forward,” said North Dakota GOP Sen. Kevin Cramer. “But I also don't begrudge them for their opinions and their right to be open about them.”

These outgoing Republicans, several of whom were explicitly pushed out by Trump or persuaded to retire given his hold on the GOP, are using the midterms as a test: whether the party will demand loyalty to the president or can return to a pre-Trump era.

“What [Trump’s] done is created a coalition that, in my opinion, will not stay with Republicans once we go back to traditional Republican platform priorities,” Tillis said in a recent interview with POLITICO . “A lot of the elements of the populism that Trump created to expand a base that made him successful running for president, I don't think that stays with the party long-term.”

Some of those intraparty frustrations are starting to boil over, with Trump loyalist candidates and outgoing Republicans swiping at one another as Election Day barrels closer and the party’s overall fortunes look dire. The blame game is especially prominent in some of the Senate battlegrounds where Republicans have begun to quietly retreat in the final stretch of the midterms.

Tillis never followed through on his offers to help Whatley by reaching out to holdout donors in the North Carolina Senate race, said one person familiar with the campaign who was granted anonymity to speak candidly about internal matters.

"He was never part of our strategy because ... I mean, if he could have been helpful to us, then he could have ran," the person said, referring to Tillis' decision not to seek reelection last year. "The Tillis of the past year ain’t the same guy who worked overtime to help elect Republican majorities here in NC back in 2010."

One person with knowledge of Tillis and North Carolina politics, also granted anonymity to speak candidly, countered that the outgoing GOP senator “doesn’t help sure winners or sure losers" and "Whatley has been a sure loser throughout 2026, running as Donald Trump’s ‘guy,’ and making zero effort to build his own brand."

"All Whatley had to do was to keep this race competitive, but instead the party is facing a potential wipeout. This is an embarrassing effort by a former RNC chairman who only has himself and his consultants to blame for the completely avoidable beat down coming on Nov. 3," the person added.
Spokespeople for Tillis did not respond to a request for comment. Whatley's campaign declined to comment.

Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee, touted the president’s endorsement record in a statement. More pointedly, she said that “Republicans who chose not to help elect other Republicans may as well be helping Democrats.”
The White House did not respond to a request for comment.
While the dynamic is less pronounced on the House side — Reps. Don Bacon and Elise Stefanik have been helpful to the Republicans running to replace them — there’s a clear exception: Amodei.

Flippo, who’s trying to replace him, has dealt with a host of scandals, from stolen valor accusations to carpetbagging to campaign finance issues , but Trump’s endorsement helped boost him through the Republican primary in June . Top Republican outside groups, including Club for Growth, have poured millions into his race in Nevada’s 2nd District to rescue a seat the president won by 14 points in 2024.
Amodei said in an interview that whoever was advising Trump to jump in and endorse Flippo gave “awful advice.”
body_zh: 被唐纳德·特朗普总统抛弃的共和党人对拯救他们的潜在继任者不感兴趣。
相反，从内华达州到北卡罗来纳州，越来越多退休或被赶下台的共和党现任议员拒绝参加这些竞选，在某些情况下，还公开反对自己的政党。
即将离任的参议员约翰·科宁 (John Cornyn) 为多位共和党参议院候选人筹集了资金，但没有为德克萨斯州总检察长肯·帕克斯顿 (Ken Paxton) 筹集资金，后者在特朗普的支持下在初选中将他赶下台。几个月来，他一直直言不讳地谈论帕克斯顿的弱点，以及民主党如何能够在几十年来首次将德克萨斯州变成蓝色。
北卡罗来纳州参议员汤姆·蒂利斯（Thom Tillis）经常批评特朗普的一些内阁成员，并在政策上与白宫决裂。他在特朗普精心挑选的参议院候选人、共和党全国委员会前主席迈克尔·沃特利（Michael Whatley）的竞选活动中几乎没有发挥任何作用。由于沃特利正在努力缩小与民主党人罗伊·库珀的差距，两位共和党人之间的差距尤其引人注目。
众议员马克·阿莫迪 (Mark Amodei) 曾多次批评并公开拒绝投票给取代他的共和党提名人大卫·弗利波 (David Flippo)。
“即将离任的温和派共和党人的尿床将决定他们的政治遗产，并且只会帮助社会主义者当选，”与特朗普结盟的增长俱乐部主席戴维·麦金托什(David McIntosh)表示，该俱乐部支持弗利波和帕克斯顿。 “像 John Cornyn 和 Mark Amodei 这样的人需要加入并支持共和党提名人，并停止摆出争取 MSNOW 合同的姿态。”
但其他共和党人为他们的同事辩护：“我永远不会质疑汤姆·蒂利斯或约翰·科宁对政党的忠诚度。他们两人都为我们的政党以及我们政党过去的成功做出了巨大贡献，我怀疑他们将来也会继续前进，”北达科他州共和党参议员凯文·克莱默说。 “但我也不嫉妒他们的观点以及他们公开表达观点的权利。”
这些即将离任的共和党人，其中一些人被特朗普明确排挤，或者由于特朗普对共和党的控制而被说服退休，他们正在利用中期选举作为考验：共和党是否会要求效忠总统，或者能否回到特朗普之前的时代。
蒂利斯最近在接受《政治》杂志采访时表示：“我认为，一旦我们回到传统的共和党政纲优先事项，特朗普所做的就是创建一个联盟，这个联盟不会与共和党保持一致。” “特朗普为扩大选民基础而创造的许多民粹主义元素，使他成功竞选总统，但我认为这些元素不会长期存在于该党之中。”
随着选举日的临近，党内的一些不满情绪开始沸腾，特朗普的忠实候选人和即将卸任的共和党人互相攻击，而该党的整体命运看起来很糟糕。指责游戏在参议院的一些战场上尤其突出，共和党人在中期选举的最后阶段开始悄悄撤退。
一位熟悉竞选活动的人士表示，蒂利斯从未兑现他向北卡罗来纳州参议员竞选中坚持不懈的捐助者来帮助沃特利的提议，该人士被要求匿名坦率地谈论内部事务。
“他从来都不是我们战略的一部分，因为……我的意思是，如果他能够对我们有帮助，那么他就可以参选，”该人士说，他指的是蒂利斯去年决定不寻求连任。 “去年的蒂利斯与 2010 年加班加点帮助共和党在北卡罗来纳州选举多数席位的人已经不一样了。”
一位了解蒂利斯和北卡罗来纳州政治的人士也不愿透露姓名，他坦率地反驳说，即将离任的共和党参议员“无助于确定的赢家或输家”，并且“沃特利在整个 2026 年都是肯定的输家，作为唐纳德·特朗普的‘人’竞选，并为打造自己的品牌做出了零努力。”
“沃特利所要做的就是保持这场竞选的竞争力，但该党却面临着潜在的全军覆没。这是一位前共和党全国委员会主席的令人尴尬的举动，他只能将 11 月 3 日完全可以避免的失败归咎于他自己和他的顾问，”该人士补充道。
蒂利斯的发言人没有回应置评请求。沃特利的竞选团队拒绝发表评论。
共和党全国委员会发言人娜塔莉·巴尔达萨尔在一份声明中赞扬了总统的支持记录。更尖锐的是，她说“选择不帮助选举其他共和党人的共和党人也可能在帮助民主党人。”
白宫没有回应置评请求。
虽然众议院方面的动态不太明显——众议员唐·培根和埃莉斯·斯特凡尼克一直在帮助共和党竞选取代他们——但有一个明显的例外：阿莫代。
试图取代他的弗利波曾处理过一系列丑闻，从盗窃勇气指控到走私行为，再到竞选财务问题，但特朗普的支持帮助他在六月份的共和党初选中脱颖而出。包括增长俱乐部在内的顶级共和党外部团体已投入数百万美元参加他在内华达州第二选区的竞选，以挽救总统在 2024 年以 14 个百分点赢得的席位。
阿莫代在接受采访时表示，无论是谁建议特朗普加入并支持 Flippo，都给出了“糟糕的建议”。

title_en: Trump administration charges former FBI Director James Comey for the third time
title_zh: 特朗普政府第三次指控前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米
summary: The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey for what it calls disclosing classified information, employing the unusual maneuver of bypassing a grand jury.
summary_zh: 特朗普政府正试图起诉前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米，罪名是泄露机密信息。
body_en: Trump administration charges former FBI Director James Comey for the third time | PBS News
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-administration-charges-former-fbi-director-james-comey-for-the-third-time
Trump administration charges former FBI Director James Comey for the third time
Politics Updated on Oct 26, 2026 6:47 PM EDT — Published on Oct 26, 2026 6:01 PM EDT

WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute James Comey for what it calls a decade-old leak of classified information, an effort the former FBI director's lawyers immediately dismissed as invalid and outside the legal time limit for when the Justice Department can file a criminal indictment.

The allegations from the Justice Department were revealed Monday in newly unsealed court documents that shed light on a closed-door fight that represents a clear escalation in the administration's targeting of Comey , a longtime critic and foe of President Donald Trump who has faced two other criminal cases since the Republican returned to the White House last year. The effort to prosecute Comey is also part of a series of politically charged investigative actions the department has undertaken in the run-up to next week's midterm elections.

"Well, they're back — again," Comey said in a video statement released after the documents dropped. "It would almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice – one that we cannot become numb to. Nothing's changed with me; I'm still innocent, I'm still not afraid of these people — and I still believe in an independent federal judiciary."
The Justice Department, for its part, said it had filed what's known as a "criminal information" to extend the 10-year statute of limitations for bringing a case.

"Filing a criminal information to toll the statute of limitations is a widely recognized practice in federal court and has been approved by multiple Circuit Courts of Appeals. This is an ongoing criminal investigation, and we will not comment further," a department spokesperson said.

A criminal information is typically filed with a defendant's consent accompanying a plea deal, but Comey's lawyers made clear that they intend to fight the charges as invalid and barred by the statute of limitations.

"For the third time in little more than one year, the Department of Justice has attempted to charge Mr. Comey with a federal crime. Mr. Comey steadfastly maintains his innocence," his attorney, Patrick Fitzgerald, said in a statement.

The latest allegation concerns an October 2016 New York Times story related to a secret court order that required Yahoo to scan emails for messages potentially linked to a foreign terrorist organization. The story cited two government officials who spoke on the condition of anonymity about the order from a judge on the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court that Yahoo was barred from publicly disclosing.

Federal authorities, including then-Special Counsel John Durham, began investigating the FBI's Oct. 5, 2016, disclosure to The New York Times in early 2017. Durham wrote a classified memo in December 2018 recommending no criminal charges against anyone in connection with the disclosure, Comey's attorneys said in a recent court filing.

In January 2019, the U.S. Attorney's office for the District of Columbia opened a second investigation of the same matter under the code name "Tropical Vortex." But that investigation was closed without any charges filed in February 2020.

"Both times the Government determined that no charges should be brought against anyone. Now, ten years after the article was published, the Government filed an "Information" against Mr. Comey that was not approved by a judge nor issued by a grand jury. It purports to charge Mr. Comey with crimes that he did not commit," Fitzgerald said.
Trump and Comey have a long and uneasy history

The first case against Comey was dismissed after the judge found that the prosecutor who brought the indictment was illegally appointed. Comey was charged in a separate case in April over a social media post depicting seashells on the beach that officials said constituted a threat against the president.

Comey was the FBI director when Trump took office in 2017, having been appointed by then-President Barack Obama, a Democrat, and serving before that as a senior Justice Department official in President George W. Bush's Republican administration.

But the relationship was strained from the start, including after Comey resisted a request by Trump at a private dinner to pledge his personal loyalty to the president -- an overture that so unnerved the FBI director that he documented it in a contemporaneous memorandum.

Trump fired Comey in May 2017 amid an FBI investigation into potential ties between Russia and Trump's campaign. That inquiry, later taken over by special counsel Robert Mueller, found that while Russia interfered in the 2016 election and the Trump team welcomed the help, there was insufficient evidence to prove a criminal collaboration.
body_zh: 特朗普政府第三次指控前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米美国公共广播公司新闻
特朗普政府第三次指控前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米
政治更新于美国东部时间 2026 年 10 月 26 日下午 6:47 — 发布于美国东部时间 2026 年 10 月 26 日下午 6:01
华盛顿（美联社）——特朗普政府正试图以十年前泄露机密信息为由起诉詹姆斯·科米，这位前联邦调查局局长的律师立即驳回了这一努力，称其无效，而且超出了司法部提起刑事起诉的法定时限。
司法部的指控在周一新公布的法庭文件中披露，这些文件揭示了一场闭门斗争，这表明政府针对科米的攻击明显升级。科米是唐纳德·特朗普总统的长期批评者和敌人，自去年共和党重返白宫以来，科米还面临另外两起刑事案件。起诉科米的努力也是该部门在下周中期选举前夕采取的一系列政治调查行动的一部分。
“好吧，他们又回来了，”科米在文件掉落后发布的视频声明中说道。 “如果这不是司法部如此令人震惊的滥用行为，那几乎会很有趣——我们不能对此麻木不仁。我什么都没有改变；我仍然是无辜的，我仍然不怕这些人——而且我仍然相信独立的联邦司法机构。”
司法部则表示，已提交所谓的“犯罪信息”，以延长提起诉讼的 10 年时效。
“提交犯罪信息以延长诉讼时效是联邦法院广泛认可的做法，并已得到多个巡回上诉法院的批准。这是一项正在进行的刑事调查，我们不会进一步发表评论，”部门发言人表示。
犯罪信息通常是在被告同意并附有认罪协议的情况下提交的，但科米的律师明确表示，他们打算将这些指控视为无效并受到时效限制。
“司法部在一年多的时间里第三次试图指控科米先生犯有联邦罪行。科米先生坚定地坚称自己无罪，”他的律师帕特里克·菲茨杰拉德在一份声明中表示。
最新指控涉及《纽约时报》2016 年 10 月的一篇报道，该报道涉及一项秘密法庭命令，该命令要求雅虎扫描电子邮件以查找可能与外国恐怖组织有关的消息。该报道援引了两名不愿透露姓名的政府官员的话说，他们谈到了外国情报监视法院一名法官下达的禁止雅虎公开披露的命令。
包括当时的特别顾问约翰·达勒姆在内的联邦当局于 2017 年初开始调查联邦调查局 2016 年 10 月 5 日向《纽约时报》披露的信息。科米的律师在最近的一份法庭文件中表示，达勒姆于 2018 年 12 月撰写了一份机密备忘录，建议不对与该披露有关的任何人提出刑事指控。
2019 年 1 月，美国哥伦比亚特区检察官办公室以“热带涡旋”为代号对同一事件展开第二次调查。但该调查于 2020 年 2 月结束，未提出任何指控。
“两次政府都决定不应对任何人提出指控。现在，在该文章发表十年后，政府向科米先生提交了一份“信息”，该信息未经法官批准，也未经大陪审团发布。它旨在指控科米先生犯下他没有犯下的罪行，”菲茨杰拉德说。
特朗普和科米有着悠久而不安的历史
在法官发现提出起诉的检察官是非法任命后，针对科米的第一起案件被驳回。科米四月份在另一起案件中受到指控，原因是社交媒体上发布了一篇描绘海滩上贝壳的帖子，官员们称该帖子对总统构成了威胁。
科米于 2017 年特朗普上任时担任联邦调查局局长，由当时的民主党总统巴拉克·奥巴马任命，此前曾在乔治·W·布什总统的共和党政府中担任司法部高级官员。
但两国关系从一开始就很紧张，包括科米在一次私人晚宴上拒绝了特朗普承诺个人忠诚于总统的要求之后——这一提议让这位联邦调查局局长感到非常不安，以至于他将其记录在了同期的备忘录中。
2017 年 5 月，在联邦调查局 (FBI) 调查俄罗斯与特朗普竞选团队之间的潜在关系期间，特朗普解雇了科米。这项调查后来由特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒 (Robert Mueller) 接管，调查发现，虽然俄罗斯干预了 2016 年大选，特朗普团队也欢迎这种帮助，但没有足够的证据证明存在犯罪勾结。

title_en: Trump administration asks Washington state to set aside ballots from 400 voters it says may be noncitizens
title_zh: 特朗普政府要求华盛顿州搁置 400 名可能是非公民选民的选票
summary: The effort is the latest by the administration to identify noncitizen voters, even though noncitizen voting is exceptionally rare.

body_en: Trump administration asks Washington state to set aside ballots from 400 voters it says may be noncitizens | PBS News
Gene Johnson, Associated Press Gene Johnson, Associated Press
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-administration-asks-washington-state-to-set-aside-ballots-from-400-voters-it-says-may-be-noncitizens
Trump administration asks Washington state to set aside ballots from 400 voters it says may be noncitizens
SEATTLE (AP) — The Trump administration on Monday asked Washington state to set aside any ballots received from more than 400 people it suspects registered to vote without U.S. citizenship.

In a letter to the Washington Secretary of State's Office, the Justice Department said it had identified 1,500 votes cast by the over 400 people in prior elections. It asked the state to set aside any ballots the people might cast in next month's midterm until state officials can confirm they are legally eligible to vote. The state has more than 5 million registered voters.
"We are asking the state to set aside those ballots until we can confirm they are legal voters," Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd said in a news conference.

Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs was reviewing the administration's demand. His office noted that it had received about 60 subpoenas from the Justice Department since last month seeking information about voters.

"We take our responsibility to protect voter information seriously and will only respond to requests that follow due process," Hobbs said in an emailed statement. "We see what's happening in California and don't want Washingtonians to be harassed."

The effort is the latest by the administration to identify noncitizen voters, even though noncitizen voting is exceptionally rare. President Donald Trump has repeatedly sought to undermine public confidence in elections. The request in Washington is similar to Justice Department attempt to require California to sequester mail ballots from up to 20,000 people the federal government suspects may not be citizens.

California has challenged that, and during rare Sunday arguments a panel of federal appellate judges questioned the timing, constitutionality and authority of the Justice Department's demand. The Elections Clause of the U.S. Constitution gives state legislatures the power to set the time, place and manner of congressional elections.

Los Angeles County Assistant Registrar-Recorder Monica Flores said in a court filing that her staff went through a sample of 200 records from the Trump administration's list. They found the sample included canceled or inactive registrations, people with no voting history and voters who appeared to have been born in the United States.

The Justice Department told Washington it anticipates sending the state an additional list of people it suspects are not citizens prior to Election Day. It also noted that some of the people it suspects registered without citizenship may have since become naturalized.

Investigations into prior allegations of noncitizen voters have revealed far fewer instances than the Trump administration has claimed. In Nevada, Trump's administration alleged there were 1,500 potential noncitizen voters on the rolls but subsequent investigation found zero.

In Maricopa County, which includes Phoenix, the county Recorder, who is a Trump supporter, announced that there were 207 possible noncitizens on the county's rolls. The Republican County Attorney determined there were actually eight.

特朗普政府要求华盛顿州搁置 400 名可能是非公民选民的选票
西雅图（美联社）——特朗普政府周一要求华盛顿州搁置其怀疑登记投票的 400 多名非美国公民的选票。
司法部在致华盛顿国务卿办公室的一封信中表示，已确定了 400 多人在之前选举中投出的 1,500 张选票。它要求该州搁置人民在下个月的中期选举中可能投票的任何选票，直到州官员确认他们有合法投票资格。该州有超过 500 万登记选民。
美国代理检察官尼尔·弗洛伊德在新闻发布会上说：“我们要求州政府搁置这些选票，直到我们确认他们是合法选民。”
华盛顿国务卿史蒂夫·霍布斯正在审查政府的要求。他的办公室指出，自上个月以来，已收到司法部约 60 张传票，寻求有关选民的信息。
霍布斯在一份电子邮件声明中表示：“我们有责任认真保护选民信息，并且只会回应遵循正当程序的请求。” “我们看到加州正在发生的事情，不希望华盛顿人受到骚扰。”
这是政府识别非公民选民身份的最新举措，尽管非公民投票的情况极其罕见。唐纳德·特朗普总统一再试图削弱公众对选举的信心。华盛顿的请求类似于司法部试图要求加州扣押联邦政府怀疑可能不是公民的多达 20,000 人的邮寄选票。
加州对此提出了质疑，在周日罕见的辩论中，联邦上诉法官小组对司法部要求的时机、合宪性和权威提出了质疑。美国宪法的选举条款赋予州立法机关确定国会选举时间、地点和方式的权力。
洛杉矶县助理登记员莫妮卡·弗洛雷斯 (Monica Flores) 在一份法庭文件中表示，她的工作人员从特朗普政府的名单中抽取了 200 条记录样本。他们发现样本包括取消或不活跃的登记、没有投票历史的人以及似乎出生在美国的选民。
司法部告诉华盛顿，预计将在选举日之前向该州发送一份怀疑不是公民的额外名单。它还指出，一些它怀疑登记为无公民身份的人可能已经入籍。
对之前针对非公民选民的指控的调查显示，实际情况比特朗普政府声称的要少得多。在内华达州，特朗普政府声称名单上有 1,500 名潜在的非公民选民，但随后的调查发现为零。
在包括菲尼克斯在内的马里科帕县，作为特朗普支持者的县记录员宣布，该县的名单上可能有 207 名非公民。共和党县检察官确定实际上有八个。

title_en: Blakeman’s bank statements don’t match his disclosure reports
title_zh: 布莱克曼的银行对账单与他的披露报告不符
body_en: 🚨🚨MUST READ🚨🚨: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and a group of fellow basketball enthusiasts have been secretly using the NYPD Police Academy’s gymnasium in Queens to play pickup ball, according to four people familiar with the games. The mayor and his crew typically show up around 10 or 11 p.m. and enter surreptitiously through a loading dock before hitting the court. While sports fanaticism has often buoyed the political brand of past mayors, Mamdani’s choice of venue is raising eyebrows. Read the story from POLITICO’s Graham Rayman, Chris Sommerfeldt and Joe Anuta here .

FINANCE FLAWS: Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman’s campaign finance disclosure reports have been plagued by inaccuracies since the spring. Copies of the campaign’s bank statements obtained by POLITICO suggest his filings might have even more problems than previously suspected.
According to a disclosure report submitted to the state Board of Elections earlier this month, the Blakeman campaign had only $178,000 in the bank as of Sept. 28.
Yet the campaign’s checking account had a balance of $1.7 million on Sept. 28, according to TD Bank’s monthly statement.
The bank records also show dozens of transactions that are missing from his campaign finance filings.

On July 29, for example, the bank statements identified the campaign using a check with the number 1156 to make a $13,500 payment to an unspecified recipient. Yet Blakeman’s campaign finance reports do not identify any transactions that used check number 1156. It also hasn’t shown a single payment totaling $13,500 at any point over the past year.

In addition, there are instances in which the bank records show apparent contributions to the campaign that never show up in the disclosure reports. The statements show Blakeman was wired $18,000 by actress Lois Robbins on Sept. 2, for example, while the filings don’t show any transactions totaling $18,000 within two weeks of that date or any donations from Robbins. An $18,000 wire from attorney and campaign finance chair Howard Fensterman in July similarly doesn’t match anything in the disclosure reports.

Blakeman is the first gubernatorial candidate in state history to participate in the new matching funds program that lets him receive up to $3.5 million in public money. Then-Mayor Eric Adams was blocked from participating in a similar New York City program last year due to discrepancies between his bank statements and disclosure reports.
Reinvent Albany’s Kyle Kennedy said he didn’t know the cause of the discrepancies, but that it could just be due to “the timing of when things were recorded.”
But, he noted, Blakeman’s campaign “will automatically be audited by the Board of Elections after the election. … Campaign finance enforcement takes place after elections, not in real-time.”
Blakeman’s campaign didn’t respond to a request to explain the discrepancies. It has previously said its campaign finance problems are due to technical issues caused by a large number of donors.

Several of the candidate’s campaign finance disclosure reports have been repeatedly amended, often in ways that made the initial numbers wildly inaccurate. His July report showed him with $4.7 million in the bank; that was changed a week later to show his balance was $6.1 million; then in August it was changed to $4.3 million.

As POLITICO reported earlier this month , Blakeman has received about $360,000 in donations over the contribution limit that he still needs to return. Many of the donations he has already returned have been highly unusual — one person who gave $1 in July was quickly refunded $780.76.
His campaign then said he accidentally submitted some duplicate contributions. Nearly a month later, it hasn’t amended the filing to show which transactions were real.
And as New York Focus reported , the Blakeman campaign submitted requests to receive matching funds for 2,600 donations that were ineligible for matches.
THE WEEKEND TURNOUT: Early voting turnout has skyrocketed in every corner of the state, according to unofficial tallies provided by the state Board of Elections.
On the first two days of early voting in 2022, 261,735 people cast a ballot. This weekend, that number increased to 485,205 — a jump of roughly 85 percent.

The biggest increases were in the North Country — particularly in the congressional seat being vacated by Rep. Elise Stefanik, which is now a battleground district for the first time in over a decade. Washington County’s weekend turnout was up 236 percent from four years ago. Early voting increased 196 percent in St. Lawrence County, 182 percent in Warren County, and 179 percent in Herkimer County.

The smallest gains were in the Hudson Valley. That was especially true in the district held by Democratic Rep. Pat Ryan, where early turnout was the highest in the state four years ago as Ryan won his first full term in a nail-biter. His race isn’t widely viewed as competitive this year, and the smallest increase among the state’s 62 counties was in Ulster, which was up only 41 percent relative to 2022.

There were also relatively middling gains in Erie County (up 60 percent) and Nassau County (up 64 percent). Those are the places where New York’s two gubernatorial candidates live, perhaps indicating that neither is yet the beneficiary of any outpourings of hometown pride. — Bill Mahoney
body_zh: 🚨🚨必读🚨🚨：据四位知情人士透露，市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 和一群篮球爱好者一直在秘密使用皇后区纽约警察学院警察学院的体育馆打皮球。市长和他的工作人员通常在晚上 10 点或 11 点左右出现。并在上场之前通过装卸码头秘密进入。虽然体育狂热经常提振前任市长的政治形象，但马姆达尼对场地的选择却令人惊讶。请阅读 POLITICO 的 Graham Rayman、Chris Sommerfeldt 和 Joe Anuta 的故事。
财务缺陷：自春季以来，共和党州长候选人布鲁斯·布莱克曼的竞选财务披露报告一直存在不准确的问题。 《政治》杂志获得的竞选银行对账单副本表明，他的文件可能存在比之前怀疑的更多问题。
根据本月早些时候提交给州选举委员会的一份披露报告，截至 9 月 28 日，布莱克曼竞选团队的银行存款只有 178,000 美元。
然而，根据道明银行的月度报表，截至 9 月 28 日，该活动的支票账户余额为 170 万美元。
银行记录还显示了他的竞选财务文件中缺失的数十笔交易。
例如，7 月 29 日，银行对账单显示该活动使用编号为 1156 的支票向未指定的收款人支付了 13,500 美元。然而，布莱克曼的竞选财务报告并未发现任何使用 1156 号支票的交易。它也没有显示过去一年中任何时候总计 13,500 美元的单笔付款。

此外，在某些情况下，银行记录显示对该活动的明显贡献从未出现在披露报告中。例如，声明显示布莱克曼在 9 月 2 日被女演员洛伊丝·罗宾斯 (Lois Robbins) 电汇了 18,000 美元，但文件并未显示该日期后两周内发生的任何总计 18,000 美元的交易，也没有来自罗宾斯的任何捐赠。 7 月份，律师兼竞选财务主席霍华德·芬斯特曼 (Howard Fensterman) 发来的 18,000 美元电汇同样与披露报告中的任何内容都不相符。
布莱克曼是该州历史上第一位参与新配套资金计划的州长候选人，该计划使他能够获得高达 350 万美元的公共资金。去年，时任市长埃里克·亚当斯（Eric Adams）因银行对账单与披露报告之间存在差异而被禁止参与纽约市的类似计划。
Reinvent Albany 的凯尔·肯尼迪表示，他不知道差异的原因，但这可能只是由于“记录事物的时间”造成的。
但是，他指出，布莱克曼的竞选活动“将在选举后自动接受选举委员会的审计。……竞选财务的执行是在选举后进行的，而不是实时进行的。”
布莱克曼的竞选团队没有回应解释这些差异的请求。它此前曾表示，其竞选财务问题是由于大量捐助者造成的技术问题造成的。
几份候选人的竞选财务披露报告已被反复修改，其修改方式往往导致最初的数字极不准确。他 7 月份的报告显示，他的银行存款为 470 万美元；一周后更改显示他的余额为 610 万美元；然后在8月份改为430万美元。
据 POLITICO 本月早些时候报道，布莱克曼已收到超过捐款限额的约 36 万美元捐款，但他仍需要归还。他已经退还的许多捐款都非常不寻常——一个人在 7 月份捐赠了 1 美元，很快就被退还了 780.76 美元。
他的竞选团队随后表示，他不小心提交了一些重复的捐款。近一个月后，它尚未修改文件以显示哪些交易是真实的。
据《纽约焦点》报道，布莱克曼竞选团队提交了为 2,600 笔不符合配捐资格的捐款接收配捐资金的请求。
周末投票率：根据州选举委员会提供的非官方统计数据，该州各个角落的提前投票投票率都在飙升。
2022 年提前投票的前两天，共有 261,735 人投票。本周末，这一数字增至 485,205 人，增幅约为 85%。
增幅最大的是北部地区，尤其是众议员埃莉斯·斯特凡尼克(Elise Stefanik)空出的国会席位，该地区十多年来首次成为战场地区。华盛顿县周末投票率比四年前增加了 236%。圣劳伦斯县的提前投票率增加了 196%，沃伦县的提前投票率增加了 182%，赫基默县的提前投票率增加了 179%。
涨幅最小的是哈德逊河谷。在民主党众议员帕特·瑞安 (Pat Ryan) 控制的选区尤其如此，四年前，瑞安以艰难的方式赢得了他的第一个完整任期，该选区的早期投票率是该州最高的。人们普遍认为今年他的竞选竞争并不激烈，该州 62 个县中增幅最小的是阿尔斯特省，与 2022 年相比仅增长了 41%。
伊利县（增长 60%）和拿骚县（增长 64%）的增幅也相对中等。这些是纽约两位州长候选人居住的地方，也许表明他们都还没有从家乡自豪感中受益。 — 比尔·马奥尼

title_en: Trump allies fall in two elections as Netanyahu faces next test
title_zh: 特朗普的盟友在两次选举中落败，内塔尼亚胡面临下一个考验
summary: A pair of Trump-friendly, right-wing populists took a one-two punch Sunday: Brazil rejected a Bolsonaro comeback, and Serbia toppled a strongman's ruling party. The big picture: Brazil denied Trump a close ally at the helm of Latin America's largest economy, s
summary_zh: 周日，一对对特朗普友好的右翼民粹主义者以一比二的方式出拳：巴西拒绝了博尔索纳罗的复出，塞尔维亚推翻了强人的统治
body_en: A pair of Trump-friendly, right-wing populists took a one-two punch Sunday: Brazil rejected a Bolsonaro comeback, and Serbia toppled a strongman's ruling party.

The big picture: Brazil denied Trump a close ally at the helm of Latin America's largest economy, snapping a streak of seven straight conservative wins in the region. In Europe, Serbia and Hungary toppled leaders with close Trump ties who had dominated their countries for years.
Another massively pivotal election looms Tuesday, when Trump ally , Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, will face a battle for political survival .

On the eve of the election, Netanyahu touted Trump's endorsement and his "friendship" with the American president. But as the global right has made gains, opposition forces proved this weekend that they still have fuel.
Driving the news: In Brazil, leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva staved off a challenge from Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro .
The younger Bolsonaro, widely seen as the heir to his father's populist movement, refused to concede and called for the results to be annulled, according to translations .
The elder Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year sentence after being convicted of plotting a coup to overturn his 2022 loss . Trump has called the prosecution a "WITCH HUNT."
The White House did not immediately respond to Axios' request for comment on the race.
Between the lines: Brazil's election emerged as a test of Trump's political influence in Latin America, where right-wing and Trump-backed candidates have celebrated an uninterrupted series of wins .
Those victories include Trump-endorsed Abelardo de la Espriella in Colombia , Nasry "Tito" Asfura in Honduras and José Antonio Kast in Chile .

Trump did not formally endorse Flávio Bolsonaro, but he met with him earlier this year and imposed significant tariffs on Brazil as he protested the charges against Bolsonaro's father. Lula is a vocal Trump critic.

In March, Flávio Bolsonaro told an audience at the Conservative Political Action Conference that America faced a "fork in the road" in the election: "Either you have the most powerful ally in the hemisphere or an antagonist."

Zoom out: Meanwhile, across the Atlantic, a student-led opposition movement in Serbia toppled the right-wing party of long-serving strongman Aleksandar Vučić, who was seeking to become prime minister.
Unlike the Bolsonaros, Vučić conceded defeat Sunday.
The Balkan leader had courted Trump's inner circle, including Donald Trump Jr. , and he described the president as a "kindred spirit."

It reflects the shifting tides that also allowed next-door Hungary to oust Trump-allied Viktor Orbán , once one of the Western world's most entrenched populist leaders, in April after 16 years in power.
Yes, but: Europe's political upheaval is cutting both ways: While the populist right has fallen in Serbia and Hungary, it's gaining ground in two of the continent's largest economies.
In France, far-right presidential front-runner Marine Le Pen launched her 2027 campaign this weekend, seizing on nationwide unrest to pitch her tough-on-crime, anti-migrant agenda.
In Germany, the far-right Alternative for Germany won a record 44% in a state election last month and continues to lead in national polls.
What we're watching: Trump's historic move of endorsing Netanyahu in Tuesday's Israeli elections will once again test his influence abroad.
body_zh: 周日，一对对特朗普友好的右翼民粹主义者遭到了一对二的打击：巴西拒绝了博尔索纳罗的复出，塞尔维亚推翻了强人的执政党。
总体情况：巴西拒绝与特朗普成为掌舵拉丁美洲最大经济体的亲密盟友，结束了保守派在该地区的七连胜。在欧洲，塞尔维亚和匈牙利推翻了与特朗普关系密切的领导人，这些领导人多年来一直统治着他们的国家。
周二，另一场重大选举即将到来，届时特朗普的盟友、以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡将面临一场政治生存之战。
选举前夕，内塔尼亚胡大肆宣扬特朗普的支持以及他与美国总统的“友谊”。但随着全球右翼势力取得进展，反对派力量本周末证明他们仍然有燃料。
推动新闻：在巴西，左翼总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦（Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva）抵御了前总统雅伊尔·博尔索纳罗（Jair Bolsonaro）之子弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗（Flávio Bolsonaro）的挑战。
据翻译报道，被广泛视为其父亲民粹主义运动继承人的年轻博尔索纳罗拒绝让步，并呼吁废除选举结果。
老博尔索纳罗因策划政变推翻 2022 年的失败而被定罪，目前正在服刑 27 年。特朗普称起诉是“政治迫害”。
白宫没有立即回应 Axios 对竞选发表评论的请求。
言外之意是：巴西的选举是对特朗普在拉丁美洲政治影响力的一次考验，那里的右翼和特朗普支持的候选人庆祝了一系列不间断的胜利。
这些胜利包括特朗普支持的哥伦比亚的阿韦拉多·德拉埃斯普里埃拉、洪都拉斯的纳斯里·“蒂托”·阿斯富拉和智利的何塞·安东尼奥·卡斯特。
特朗普并未正式支持弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗，但他在今年早些时候会见了他，并在抗议对博尔索纳罗父亲的指控时对巴西征收了高额关税。卢拉是特朗普的直言不讳的批评者。
今年三月，弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗在保守党政治行动会议上对观众表示，美国在选举中面临“岔路口”：“要么拥有西半球最强大的盟友，要么面临对手。”
与此同时，在大西洋彼岸，塞尔维亚学生领导的反对运动推翻了长期任职的强人亚历山大·武契奇(Aleksandar Vučić)的右翼政党，后者正在寻求成为总理。
与博索纳罗家族不同，武契奇周日承认失败。
这位巴尔干领导人向包括小唐纳德·特朗普在内的特朗普核心圈子示好，他称总统是“志同道合的人”。
它反映了潮流的转变，也使得邻国匈牙利在执政 16 年后于 4 月推翻了特朗普盟友欧尔班·维克多 (Viktor Orbán)，欧尔班曾是西方世界最根深蒂固的民粹主义领导人之一。
是的，但是：欧洲的政治动荡是双向的：虽然塞尔维亚和匈牙利的民粹主义右翼已经垮台，但它在欧洲大陆最大的两个经济体中却正在取得进展。
在法国，极右翼总统候选人马琳·勒庞本周末启动了她的2027年竞选活动，利用全国范围内的骚乱来宣传她严厉打击犯罪和反移民的议程。
在德国，极右翼的德国另类选择党在上个月的州选举中赢得了创纪录的 44%，并在全国民意调查中继续领先。
我们正在关注的是：特朗普在周二的以色列选举中支持内塔尼亚胡的历史性举动将再次考验他的海外影响力。

title_en: Trump administration pushes for food assistance card upgrade to fight fraud
title_zh: 特朗普政府推动食品援助卡升级以打击欺诈
summary: The proposed rule is a major step forward in addressing a form of fraud that has robbed SNAP recipients of millions.
summary_zh: 拟议的规则是解决导致 SNAP 受益人损失数百万美元的欺诈行为的重要一步。
body_en: Trump administration pushes to upgrade food assistance cards : NPR
Trump administration pushes to upgrade food assistance cards The proposed rule is a major step forward in addressing a form of fraud that has robbed SNAP recipients of millions.
Trump administration pushes for food assistance card upgrade to fight fraud
A SNAP recipient checks her balance left after purchasing food supplies with a California EBT card in Los Angeles on Oct. 31, 2025. Damian Dovarganes/AP hide caption

In a major step to combat a form of fraud that has robbed food stamp recipients of millions of dollars , the Trump administration is proposing a requirement for states to bolster the security features on their food assistance cards.

In recent years, the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, has been the repeated target of card skimming, when thieves extract personal information from payment terminals and drain money from accounts. Most SNAP cards rely on a magnetic stripe for swipe payment – which tends to be vulnerable to skimming because it does a poor job of securing the data stored on cards.
'They're stealing from the poor': A major source of SNAP fraud robs recipients of millions

Many banks in the U.S. took action against this issue over a decade ago by upgrading their cards to include microchips and tap-to-pay, which are considered more secure. But states have lagged in making such a transition for Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) cards, which are what SNAP recipients use to access food aid. Currently, fewer than a third of states have made the switch or are in process of doing so, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA).

Now, under the proposed rule released by the USDA last week, all states would have to adopt chip-enabled EBT cards. It also requires retailers that accept SNAP benefits to have payment terminals that support tap-pay. The USDA's Food and Nutrition Administration, which administers SNAP, attributed card skimming as a reason behind the proposal.
"These proposed changes will protect SNAP benefits from thieves and ensure benefits are accessible by approved households," the Food and Nutrition Administration said in its summary of the rule.

Back in January, the USDA Office of Inspector General projected that SNAP theft could climb to $233 million between 2025 and 2026 — largely as a result of skimming. A recent ProPublica investigation found that last year, $470 million was stolen electronically from SNAP recipients. The total was calculated using data from Propel, an app that helps SNAP recipients check their food benefits.
In most states, stolen benefits are not replaced — leaving recipients to make difficult choices, such as skipping meals or borrowing money in order to pay for groceries, according to Propel .

Earlier this month, NPR reported that food assistance card modernization had widespread support from state officials and federal watchdogs, as well as Republicans and Democrats in Congress. But money has been a major barrier for states to make the switch. According to the Government Accountability Office, chip-enabled cards are about 10 times more expensive to produce than their magnetic strip counterparts.

The federal push for stronger card security features comes as state SNAP agencies are facing new budget pressures triggered by President Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The proposed regulation recognized the financial barrier, adding that the USDA is interested in hearing from state agencies about the cost burden.
"As stewards of taxpayer dollars, the Department considers these administrative costs as a necessary investment to deter the loss of Federally-funded SNAP benefits," the proposed rule said.
Why these 5 everyday items fluctuate in price at the grocery store

The public has 60 days to submit comments on the proposal before the USDA publishes a final rule. The department is considering giving states a two-year deadline from that publication date to implement the rule, but it also welcomed input on whether that's enough time.

When asked if the department would consider providing funding to help states upgrade their card technology, the USDA said that "For years, States had access to administrative funds to stop this egregious abuse of taxpayer resources. Yet few acted."
The USDA added that the proposed rule has been in the works for nearly four years. It estimates that the changes will reduce stolen benefits by at least $1.5 billion over the next decade.

SNAP has been one of the focus areas in the Trump administration's war on fraud. Last week, the Justice Department announced that its fraud division helped uncover nearly $42 million in schemes targeting food benefits. The investigations ranged from identity theft to retailers illegally exchanging cash for food benefits.
body_zh: 特朗普政府推动升级食品援助卡：NPR
特朗普政府推动升级食品援助卡 拟议的规则是解决欺诈行为的重要一步，这种欺诈行为已导致 SNAP 受益人损失数百万美元。
特朗普政府推动食品援助卡升级以打击欺诈
2025 年 10 月 31 日，一名 SNAP 领取者在洛杉矶用加州 EBT 卡购买食品后检查剩余余额。Damian Dovarganes/美联社 隐藏标题栏
特朗普政府为打击导致食品券领取者损失数百万美元的欺诈行为迈出了重要一步，提议要求各州加强其食品援助卡的安全功能。
近年来，补充营养援助计划（SNAP）不断成为银行卡盗取的目标，窃贼从支付终端提取个人信息并从账户中盗取资金。大多数 SNAP 卡依靠磁条进行刷卡支付，而磁条往往很容易被盗取，因为它在保护卡上存储的数据方面做得很差。
“他们从穷人那里偷窃”：SNAP 欺诈的一个主要来源导致受助者损失了数百万美元
美国的许多银行十多年前就针对这个问题采取了行动，对银行卡进行了升级，添加了微芯片和感应支付功能，这些被认为更安全。但各州在电子福利转移（EBT）卡的转型方面进展缓慢，SNAP 接受者使用电子福利转移卡来获取粮食援助。据美国农业部 (USDA) 称，目前只有不到三分之一的州已经采取或正在采取这种措施。
现在，根据美国农业部上周发布的拟议规则，所有州都必须采用支持芯片的 EBT 卡。它还要求接受 SNAP 福利的零售商拥有支持感应支付的支付终端。负责管理 SNAP 的美国农业部食品和营养管理局将银行卡盗取行为视为该提案背后的原因。
美国食品和营养管理局在规则摘要中表示：“这些拟议的修改将保护 SNAP 福利免遭小偷的侵害，并确保获得批准的家庭能够获得福利。”
早在 1 月份，美国农业部监察长办公室就预测 2025 年至 2026 年间 SNAP 盗窃额可能会攀升至 2.33 亿美元，这主要是由于窃取造成的。 ProPublica 最近的一项调查发现，去年 SNAP 受益人的 4.7 亿美元被电子盗窃。总数是根据 Propel 的数据计算得出的，Propel 是一款帮助 SNAP 受益者检查其食品福利的应用程序。
据 Propel 称，在大多数州，被盗福利并没有被取代，这让领取者不得不做出艰难的选择，比如不吃饭或借钱购买杂货。
本月早些时候，美国国家公共广播电台报道称，粮食援助卡现代化得到了州官员和联邦监管机构以及国会共和党和民主党的广泛支持。但资金一直是各州做出转变的主要障碍。据政府问责办公室称，芯片卡的生产成本比磁条卡高出约 10 倍。
联邦政府推动更强的银行卡安全功能之际，各州 SNAP 机构正面临特朗普总统的一项美丽法案引发的新预算压力。拟议的法规承认了财务障碍，并补充说美国农业部有兴趣听取州机构关于成本负担的意见。
拟议规则称：“作为纳税人资金的管理者，该部门认为这些行政成本是必要的投资，以防止联邦资助的 SNAP 福利的损失。”
为什么这 5 种日常用品在杂货店的价格波动
在美国农业部发布最终规则之前，公众有 60 天的时间提交对该提案的评论。该部门正在考虑给各州一个自发布之日起两年的期限来实施该规则，但它也欢迎就这是否足够的时间提出意见。
当被问及该部门是否会考虑提供资金来帮助各州升级其卡技术时，美国农业部表示，“多年来，各州都可以利用行政资金来制止这种对纳税人资源的严重滥用。但很少有人采取行动。”
美国农业部补充说，拟议的规则已经酝酿了近四年。据估计，这些变化将在未来十年内减少至少 15 亿美元的被盗福利。
SNAP 一直是特朗普政府打击欺诈的重点领域之一。上周，司法部宣布其欺诈部门帮助破获了近 4200 万美元的针对食品福利的计划。调查范围从身份盗窃到零售商非法用现金换取食品福利。

title_en: 6 citizens sue Trump, saying media ban deprives them of news as audience stakeholders
title_zh: 6名公民起诉特朗普，称媒体禁令剥夺了他们作为受众利益相关者获得新闻的权利
summary: A new lawsuit against President Donald Trump's media ban stakes a claim for the public itself
summary_zh: 针对唐纳德·特朗普总统媒体禁令的一项新诉讼为公众本身提出了索赔
body_en: 6 citizens sue Trump, saying media ban deprives them of news as audience stakeholders
A new lawsuit against President Donald Trump's media ban stakes a claim for the public itself

In the increasingly bitter legal standoff between President Donald Trump and media outlets whose reporting he dislikes, a new and crucial third party has emerged: citizens who watch and read the news and need it to do their jobs.

A lawsuit filed Monday on behalf of six such citizens — essentially representing the wider public audience — argues that it’s not only the rights of news organizations that are violated when Trump bans them from White House premises. Even more fundamentally, the lawsuit argues, such bans violate the public’s right to independent reporting about its president and government.

“The ultimate injury here … is to the democratic public,” says the suit, filed in federal district court in New York against Trump and three key aides, including the White House chief of staff, Susie Wiles.

“The First Amendment protects the public’s right to know what its government is doing,” said Katie Fallow, deputy litigation director at the Knight First Amendment Institute, which filed the lawsuit on behalf of the plaintiffs, along with the Media Freedom & Information Access Clinic at Yale Law School.

“The White House cannot decide what information Americans receive by punishing critical reporting," Fallow said in a statement. "When the White House expels reporters because of their coverage and threatens others with expulsion, it isn’t just the press that suffers — the public loses access to independent reporting and gets something closer to government propaganda.”

The Trump administration, asked for comment on the lawsuit, responded in a statement that it attributed to an unidentified White House official: “No person may demand access to the Oval Office." It said media that peddle "misinformation and defamation are completely capable of reporting their manufactured stories from directly outside.”

The six plaintiffs are all people who say they rely on independent and diverse White House reporting for their teaching, journalism or advocacy. They include a noted human rights advocate, a political journalist, a Yale history professor, a high school civics teacher, a legal journalist, and a student journalist at the University of Pennsylvania.

The complaint filed Monday recounts how various news organizations that have been targeted by Trump are already battling the administration in the courts. These cases include the current lawsuit by CNN, MS NOW and Politico, whose journalists were banished from the White House in September.

A federal judge recently extended an order preventing the White House from enforcing the ban while the case makes its way through the legal system. Still affected, though, is CNN’s pool coverage of Trump. The White House has been denying the network its usual slots in the video pool covering the president’s activities and travel, and CNN has threatened further action.

Also continuing is the legal case involving The Associated Press, whose reporters were barred last year from the Oval Office, Air Force One and some events in retaliation for the outlet’s decision not to follow Trump’s lead in changing the name of the Gulf of Mexico, which lies partially in Mexican and other waters, to the Gulf of America.

The New York Times is also involved in litigation, over a Pentagon policy requiring escorts for journalists on its grounds. And ABC is fighting back against the Trump administration in a dispute over renewal of its broadcast licenses.

The new lawsuit filed Monday, though, is different from previous legal action against the president — first, in that the plaintiffs are ordinary citizens, shifting the focus from news gatherers to news consumers, and thus implying a much larger pool of stakeholders. In addition, it seeks more wide-ranging relief.

The suit, which names Trump as defendant along with Wiles, White House Communications Director Steven Cheung, and Secret Service Director Sean M. Curran, calls not merely for reinstatement of access that has already been impacted, but for a broad injunction that would protect from retaliation every news outlet that covers the White House —- now, and in the future.

“Defendants' policy of restricting the access of disfavored news organizations deprives the public of the reporting of those organizations," the complaint says. It also "inevitably deprives them of the independent reporting of other news organizations as well, since every journalist who reports from the White House must now account for the possibility that a critical or ill-advised word about the president may result in their access being summarily restricted or revoked."

Britt McHenry resigns from State Department after basketball game altercation

“Plaintiffs ... seek a declaration that the policy is unconstitutional because it imposes restrictions on a limited public forum that are viewpoint-based and unreasonable," the complaint adds. "They also seek an injunction barring defendants from enforcing the policy.”
body_zh: 6名公民起诉特朗普，称媒体禁令剥夺了他们作为受众利益相关者获得新闻的权利
针对唐纳德·特朗普总统媒体禁令的一项新诉讼为公众本身提出了索赔
在唐纳德·特朗普总统与他不喜欢报道的媒体之间日益激烈的法律对峙中，一个新的、至关重要的第三方出现了：观看和阅读新闻并需要新闻来完成工作的公民。
周一代表六名此类公民（基本上代表更广泛的公众受众）提起的诉讼认为，当特朗普禁止新闻机构进入白宫时，这不仅侵犯了新闻机构的权利。诉讼称，更根本的是，此类禁令侵犯了公众独立报道总统和政府的权利。
在纽约联邦地区法院针对特朗普和包括白宫办公厅主任苏西·怀尔斯在内的三名重要助手提起的诉讼称，“这里的最终伤害……是对民主公众的伤害”。
代表原告提起诉讼的奈特第一修正案研究所副诉讼主任凯蒂·法洛（Katie Fallow）表示：“第一修正案保护公众了解政府在做什么的权利。”
法洛在一份声明中表示：“白宫无法通过惩罚批评性报道来决定美国人收到哪些信息。” “当白宫因为记者的报道而驱逐记者并威胁驱逐其他人时，受苦的不仅仅是媒体——公众失去了获得独立报道的机会，并获得了更接近政府宣传的东西。”
特朗普政府被要求对这起诉讼发表评论，并在一份声明中回应，该声明归因于一名身份不明的白宫官员：“任何人不得要求进入椭圆形办公室。”它表示，兜售“错误信息和诽谤的媒体完全有能力从外部直接报道他们捏造的故事。”
六名原告都表示，他们的教学、新闻或宣传都依赖独立且多元化的白宫报道。他们包括一位著名的人权倡导者、一位政治记者、一位耶鲁大学历史教授、一位高中公民教师、一位法律记者和一位宾夕法尼亚大学的学生记者。
周一提交的起诉书讲述了被特朗普针对的各个新闻机构如何在法庭上与政府作斗争。这些案件包括 CNN、MS NOW 和 Politico 目前提起的诉讼，这些公司的记者于 9 月被驱逐出白宫。
一名联邦法官最近发布了一项命令，阻止白宫在该案通过法律系统期间执行该禁令。不过，CNN 对特朗普的联合报道仍然受到影响。白宫一直否认该网络在报道总统活动和旅行的视频池中提供通常的时段，CNN 威胁要采取进一步行动。
同样仍在继续的还有涉及美联社的法律案件，该报记者去年被禁止进入椭圆形办公室、空军一号和一些活动，以报复该媒体决定不追随特朗普的领导，将部分位于墨西哥和其他水域的墨西哥湾更名为美洲湾。
《纽约时报》也因五角大楼要求其记者护送的政策而卷入诉讼。美国广播公司 (ABC) 正在就其广播许可证续签争议对特朗普政府进行反击。
不过，周一提起的新诉讼与之前针对总统的法律诉讼不同——首先，原告是普通公民，将焦点从新闻采集者转移到新闻消费者，从而意味着利益相关者群体要大得多。此外，它还寻求更广泛的救济。
该诉讼将特朗普与怀尔斯、白宫通讯总监史蒂文·张和特勤局局长肖恩·M·柯兰列为被告，不仅要求恢复已经受到影响的访问权限，而且要求制定一项广泛的禁令，以保护报道白宫的每个新闻媒体免受报复——无论是现在还是将来。
诉状称：“被告限制不受青睐的新闻机构访问的政策剥夺了公众对这些组织的报道。”它还“不可避免地剥夺了他们对其他新闻机构进行独立报道的权利，因为每一位从白宫进行报道的记者现在都必须考虑到这样一种可能性：对总统的批评或不明智的言论可能会导致他们的采访被立即限制或撤销。”
特朗普告诉司法部，如果共和党以微弱优势落败，将提起诉讼以阻止阿拉斯加州参议院的结果
艾米·阿克顿表示特朗普和万斯在拉马斯瓦米攻击广告后应该“看看事实”

诉状补充道：“原告……寻求一项声明，表明该政策违宪，因为它对有限的公共论坛施加了基于观点的、不合理的限制。” “他们还寻求禁令，禁止被告执行该政策。”

title_en: Fifteen-year-old arrested in shooting near Florida university that injured 12
title_zh: 佛罗里达大学附近发生枪击事件 15 岁少年被捕，造成 12 人受伤
summary: All but one of the victims sustained gunshot wounds as boy faces 11 charges of attempted second-degree murder A 15-year-old boy was remanded into secure detention in Florida on Monday charged with 11 counts of attempted murder following a mass shooting at a co
summary_zh: 除一名受害者外，所有受害者均受枪伤，男孩面临 11 项二级谋杀未遂指控 一名 15 岁男孩被还押候审
body_en: Fifteen-year-old arrested in shooting near Florida university that injured 12 | Florida
Fifteen-year-old arrested in shooting near Florida university that injured 12
All but one of the victims sustained gunshot wounds as boy faces 11 charges of attempted second-degree murder
A 15-year-old boy was remanded into secure detention in Florida on Monday charged with 11 counts of attempted murder following a mass shooting at a college homecoming party on Saturday.
Six adults and six minors were injured, all but one with gunshot wounds, in the gunfire near the Florida Agricultural + Mechanical University campus in Tallahassee.

It was among five mass shootings over the weekend – cases in which at least four victims were wounded or killed, according to the Gun Violence Archive. The archive, a nonpartisan resource, has recorded 386 such cases in the US for the year so far.
On Monday, the Tallahassee police department posted on Facebook that detectives had arrested a suspect in the shooting. The agency identified the suspect as Anthony Rivers III, 15.

Police do not typically identify criminal suspects who are minors, though the severity of the charges facing Rivers made him an exception. He faces 11 charges of attempted second-degree murder and one of possession of a firearm by a delinquent after being arrested on Sunday, police said.

Rivers appeared in juvenile court on Monday dressed in a white T-shirt and gray shorts. He was not handcuffed and did not speak during the brief hearing, during which Leon county circuit court judge Anthony Sheeran ordered him to remain in secure detention pending an arraignment.
Tallahassee police chief Lawrence Revell said in a statement that the investigation into Saturday’s shooting was ongoing, and further arrests were possible.
“What should have been a weekend of celebration in our community instead became a night of fear and violence for the victims and their families,” Revell said.

“While this arrest marks a significant step forward, our work is far from over. We remain committed to holding those responsible accountable and getting answers for every family [affected] by this tragedy.”

The department earlier said three of the victims were seriously wounded, with one in critical condition in the hospital. Nine others had gunshot wounds, the agency said – and another person injured an ankle as they attempted to escape the gunfire.

The shooting took place just before 8pm on Saturday at an intersection near the university’s Bragg stadium, where a homecoming football game had just ended. Officers were on the scene quickly and carried some of those injured to safety through a mass of people, Revell said.
According to police, Rivers opened fire after an altercation between two groups of people who were known to each other. None of those struck was believed to have been an intended target, Revell said.
Revell on Sunday thanked members of the community who had come forward with cellphone video of the shooting and its aftermath, which he said was “vital to investigative efforts”.
University president Marva Johnson posted a video message on X on Sunday condemning the “senseless and despicable” violence of the night before.

“As a neighbor and community partner, we are providing our full assistance to the Tallahassee police department,” she said. “Our pride, our identity, and our future will not be defined by the challenges we face, but how we respond to them together.”
body_zh: 佛罗里达大学附近发生枪击事件，15 岁少年被捕，造成 12 人受伤佛罗里达
佛罗里达大学附近发生枪击事件 15 岁少年被捕，造成 12 人受伤
除一名受害者外，所有受害者均受枪伤，男孩面临 11 项二级谋杀未遂指控
周六，佛罗里达州一次大学返校派对上发生大规模枪击事件，一名 15 岁男孩周一被还押在佛罗里达州安全拘留所，被指控犯有 11 项谋杀未遂罪。
塔拉哈西佛罗里达农业机械大学校园附近发生枪击事件，造成六名成人和六名未成年人受伤，其中一人受枪伤。
据枪支暴力档案馆称，这是周末发生的五起大规模枪击事件之一，其中至少四名受害者受伤或死亡。该档案是一个无党派资源，今年迄今已在美国记录了 386 起此类案件。
周一，塔拉哈西警察局在脸书上发布消息称，侦探们逮捕了枪击案的一名嫌疑人。该机构确认嫌疑人为 Anthony Rivers III，15 岁。
警方通常不会识别未成年犯罪嫌疑人，但里弗斯​​面临的指控的严重性使他成为例外。警方称，他于周日被捕后面临 11 项二级谋杀未遂指控，以及一项犯罪分子持有枪支罪的指控。
周一，里弗斯穿着白色 T 恤和灰色短裤出现在少年法庭。在简短的听证会上，他没有戴上手铐，也没有发言，在听证会上，莱昂县巡回法院法官安东尼·希兰命令他继续受到安全拘留，等待传讯。
塔拉哈西警察局长劳伦斯·雷维尔在一份声明中表示，对周六枪击事件的调查正在进行中，可能还会逮捕更多人。
雷维尔说：“我们社区本来应该庆祝的周末，却变成了受害者及其家人充满恐惧和暴力的夜晚。”
“虽然这次逮捕标志着向前迈出的重要一步，但我们的工作还远未结束。我们仍然致力于追究责任人的责任，并为每个受这场悲剧影响的家庭找到答案。”
该部门早些时候表示，三名受害者受重伤，其中一人在医院情况危急。该机构称，另外九人受枪伤，还有一人在试图逃离枪火时脚踝受伤。
枪击事件发生在周六晚上 8 点左右，地点是该大学布拉格体育场附近的一个十字路口，当时一场返校橄榄球赛刚刚结束。雷维尔说，警察迅速赶到现场，并通过人群将一些伤者转移到安全地带。
据警方称，里弗斯是在两群互相认识的人发生口角后开枪的。雷维尔说，据信没有一个被袭击的目标是预定目标。
雷维尔周日感谢社区成员提供了枪击事件及其后果的手机视频，他说这“对调查工作至关重要”。
周日，大学校长玛瓦·约翰逊在 X 上发布了一段视频，谴责前一天晚上发生的“毫无意义和卑鄙”的暴力行为。
“作为邻居和社区合作伙伴，我们正在向塔拉哈西警察局提供全力协助，”她说。 “我们的自豪感、我们的身份和我们的未来不是由我们面临的挑战决定的，而是由我们如何共同应对这些挑战决定的。”

title_en: Maurene Comey was illegally fired as federal prosecutor, judge rules
title_zh: 法官裁定莫林·科米被非法解雇联邦检察官
summary: Daughter of ex-FBI director James Comey, a Trump foe, was dismissed in 2025 despite her work being widely praised Maurene Comey , the daughter of the former FBI director James Comey , was unlawfully fired from her job as a federal prosecutor in New York last y
summary_zh: 特朗普的敌人、前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米的女儿于 2025 年被解雇，尽管她的工作受到广泛赞扬。
body_en: Maurene Comey was illegally fired as federal prosecutor, judge rules
Daughter of ex-FBI director James Comey, a Trump foe, was dismissed in 2025 despite her work being widely praised
Maurene Comey , the daughter of the former FBI director James Comey , was unlawfully fired from her job as a federal prosecutor in New York last year, a federal judge ruled on Monday.

Judge Jesse Furman said that Comey, who was an assistant US attorney for a decade, was illegally fired in July 2025 despite her work on some of the nation’s highest-profile cases and consistently receiving “the highest accolades from supervisors and peers alike”.

After her firing, Comey sued the justice department and others, saying her termination violated the constitutional separation of powers, the first amendment and the due process clause of the fifth amendment.
She asserted that she was fired because she was the daughter of James Comey , a longtime foe of Donald Trump, or because of her perceived political affiliation and beliefs, the judge noted.
How the Trump administration is trying to defend its firing of Maurene Comey
Furman rejected the government’s claim that Comey could be fired because federal prosecutors exercise the president’s “conclusive and preclusive” powers.
“The Court concludes the Defendants are wrong,” the judge wrote.
He said the government’s claim that Congress is barred from regulating the removal of federal prosecutors “flies in the face of nearly two centuries of Supreme Court precedent”.
Furman added: “Indeed, to accept Defendants’ argument would be to unsettle the very equilibrium established by this Nation’s constitutional system.”

The judge granted Comey retroactive reinstatement and back pay from the date of her firing through 20 December to “make her whole” and ensure that she doesn’t suffer adverse employment consequences for the “unlawful termination”.
Comey’s lawyers – Ellen Blain, Nicole Gueron, Deepa Vanamali and Margaret Donovan – lauded the ruling.

“This hard-earned victory belongs to Ms Comey, to all civil servants, and to all fighting for the rule of law,” they said in a statement. “As the Court correctly held, to accept the government’s argument about unlimited executive power ‘would be to unsettle the very equilibrium established by this Nation’s constitutional system.’ This decision reaffirms our bedrock system of checks and balances: the President is not above the law.”
The justice department did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment.

Under the Trump administration, the justice department has fired scores of career employees, including prosecutors and FBI agents, who participated in investigations of the president or who were perceived as opposed to the administration’s agenda. Some of those firings have also resulted in federal lawsuits .
Free speech group calls foul play at prosecutors using Comey novel in case against him
The firing of Maurene Comey was seen as particularly personal, given her father’s longtime adversarial relationship with Trump.

The president fired James Comey as FBI director in May 2017 as the bureau was investigating ties between Russia and the Republican’s successful 2016 campaign for the White House. Trump in the years since has repeatedly called for Comey to be jailed, and his justice department has worked with mixed success to make that happen.
An earlier criminal case accusing James Comey of having lied to Congress in 2020 was dismissed by a judge who concluded that the prosecutor who filed the charges was illegally appointed.

特朗普的敌人、前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米的女儿尽管工作广受好评，但仍于 2025 年被解雇
联邦法官周一裁定，前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米的女儿莫琳·科米去年被非法解雇纽约联邦检察官的职务。
杰西·弗曼法官表示，曾担任美国助理检察官十年的科米于 2025 年 7 月被非法解雇，尽管她曾处理过一些全国最引人注目的案件，并一直获得“上级和同行的最高赞誉”。
被解雇后，科米起诉司法部等人，称解雇她违反了宪法三权分立、第一修正案和第五修正案的正当程序条款。
法官指出，她声称自己被解雇是因为她是唐纳德·特朗普的长期敌人詹姆斯·科米的女儿，或者是因为她被认为的政治立场和信仰。
特朗普政府如何为解雇莫林·科米辩护
弗曼驳斥了政府关于科米可能被解雇的说法，因为联邦检察官行使总统的“决定性和排除性”权力。
“法院的结论是被告是错误的，”法官写道。
他表示，政府声称禁止国会监管联邦检察官的罢免“与最高法院近两个世纪的先例相悖”。
弗曼补充道：“事实上，接受被告的论点将破坏这个国家宪法制度所建立的平衡。”
法官批准科米从被解雇之日起至 12 月 20 日追溯恢复原职并支付欠薪，以“使她完整”，并确保她不会因“非法解雇”而遭受不利的就业后果。
科米的律师艾伦·布莱恩、妮可·盖隆、迪帕·瓦纳马利和玛格丽特·多诺万对这一裁决表示赞赏。
他们在一份声明中表示：“这一来之不易的胜利属于科米女士、属于所有公务员以及所有为法治而奋斗的人。” “正如法院正确地认为的那样，接受政府关于无限行政权力的论点‘将破坏这个国家宪法制度所建立的平衡。’这一决定重申了我们制衡的基石体系：总统并不凌驾于法律之上。”
司法部没有立即回复寻求置评的电子邮件。
在特朗普政府领导下，司法部解雇了数十名职业雇员，其中包括检察官和联邦调查局特工，他们参与了对总统的调查或被认为反对政府的议程。其中一些解雇事件还引发了联邦诉讼。
言论自由组织称检察官在针对科米的案件中使用科米小说进行了谋杀
鉴于莫琳·科米的父亲与特朗普长期以来的敌对关系，解雇莫琳·科米被认为是特别个人化的事件。
2017 年 5 月，总统解雇了联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米，当时该局正在调查俄罗斯与共和党 2016 年成功入主白宫之间的关系。此后的几年里，特朗普多次呼吁将科米投入监狱，他的司法部门为实现这一目标所做的努力，取得了不同程度的成功。
早些时候，指控詹姆斯·科米在 2020 年向国会撒谎的刑事案件被一名法官驳回，其结论是提出指控的检察官是非法任命的。

title_en: Catholic bishops regret White House prayer photo with Trump, say it was used politically
title_zh: 天主教主教对在白宫与特朗普合影表示遗憾，称其被用于政治目的
summary: Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret that they agreed to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Donald Trump
summary_zh: 两位天主教主教对同意参加一次白宫会议表示遗憾，该会议公开了他们与天主教徒一起祈祷的照片。
body_en: Catholic bishops regret White House prayer photo with Trump, say it was used politically - ABC News
Catholic bishops regret White House prayer photo with Trump, say it was used politically
Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret that they agreed to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Donald Trump
Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret about agreeing to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Donald Trump.

Milwaukee Archbishop Jeffrey Grob, in a statement titled “A Public Apology,” said Sunday that he had received many questions and comments — some of them distraught — about the meeting on Thursday which he and 11 other bishops attended.
He said the meeting was speedily publicized by the White House with photos and a video, without consent of the participants, and less than two weeks away from the midterm elections .

“I feel a heavy sadness, not only over the pain I caused, but also for the fact that something so sacred to a group of religious leaders, prayer to our Heavenly Father, would be manipulated in that way," Grob said.
The bishop of Des Moines, Iowa, William Joensen, also issued a statement making clear he felt the White House had taken advantage of the bishops.

“I wish I had been more shrewd and less simple, like those who exploited our meeting for partisan political purpose,” he wrote. “I pray I am more prudent and wise going forward, even as I remain resolute in my openness to engaging and praying for political leaders at all levels.”

Asked whether the White House had or hadn't received the bishop's consent for releasing the photos and video, the press office declined to answer that question. Instead, White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers replied, “There has never been a greater president for Catholic Americans than President Trump, and his strong record proves it."

The White House invitation to the bishops — extended in September — offered discussion about such issues as immigration enforcement, religious worker visas , abortion and use of federal tax credits to support private education, according to Joensen and Grob.

“The meeting was in no way an endorsement of the president, his policies, or his party,” wrote Grob. “We were told the meeting was to be a private discussion, that several Catholic members of the cabinet might make an appearance, and that there could be an opportunity to pray privately with the president.”
Trump told DOJ to sue to block Alaska Senate results if Republican narrowly loses
Amy Acton says Trump, Vance should 'look at the facts' after Ramaswamy attack ad
Britt McHenry resigns from State Department after basketball game altercation
“It did not take long thereafter for the White House to post a video and photos of the prayer,” Grob said.

“I soon began receiving messages of serious concern over the possibility that I had inadvertently participated in a political event less than two weeks before a national election,” he added. “I also heard from some who felt wounded because of the ways they or their family had been harmed by the president’s policies.”
“I did not go without reservations. I wish I had heeded them,” Grob concluded. “I apologize for any damage my actions have done."

Collectively, members of the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops have diverse views on Trump and his administration's policies. Minnesota-based Bishop Robert Barron, for example, agreed to serve on Trump's Religious Liberty Commission, which was filled almost entirely with conservative Christians. Some other bishops vehemently denounced aspects of Trump's tough stance on immigration enforcement , saying it runs counter to Catholic teaching.

天主教主教对在白宫与特朗普合影表示遗憾，称其被用于政治目的
两位天主教主教对同意参加一次白宫会议表示遗憾，该会议公开了他们与唐纳德·特朗普总统一起祈祷的照片
两位天主教主教对同意举行一次白宫会议表示遗憾，该会议公开了他们与唐纳德·特朗普总统一起祈祷的照片。
密尔沃基大主教杰弗里·格罗布周日在一份题为“公开道歉”的声明中表示，他收到了许多关于他和其他 11 名主教参加的周四会议的问题和评论，其中一些令人心烦意乱。
他表示，白宫在未经与会者同意的情况下，迅速用照片和视频公开了这次会议，而且距离中期选举还有不到两周的时间。
格罗布说：“我感到非常悲伤，不仅因为我造成的痛苦，还因为对一群宗教领袖来说如此神圣的事情，即向我们的天父祈祷，会被以这种方式操纵。”
爱荷华州得梅因主教威廉·约恩森也发表声明，明确表示他认为白宫利用了主教们的利益。
他写道：“我希望自己能更精明一些，不要那么简单，就像那些利用我们的会议来达到党派政治目的的人一样。” “我祈祷自己今后能更加谨慎和明智，尽管我仍然坚定地开放地参与各级政治领导人并为他们祈祷。”
当被问及白宫是否已获得主教同意发布这些照片和视频时，新闻办公室拒绝回答这个问题。相反，白宫发言人泰勒·罗杰斯回答说：“对于美国天主教徒来说，从来没有比特朗普总统更伟大的总统，他的出色记录证明了这一点。”
乔恩森和格罗布表示，白宫于九月延长了对主教的邀请，邀请他们就移民执法、宗教工作者签证、堕胎和利用联邦税收抵免支持私立教育等问题进行讨论。
格罗布写道：“这次会议绝不是对总统、他的政策或他的政党的认可。” “我们被告知，这次会议将是一次私人讨论，几位天主教内阁成员可能会出席，并且可能有机会与总统私下祈祷。”
特朗普告诉司法部，如果共和党以微弱优势落败，将提起诉讼以阻止阿拉斯加州参议院的结果
艾米·阿克顿表示特朗普和万斯在拉马斯瓦米攻击广告后应该“看看事实”
布里特·麦克亨利因篮球比赛争吵而辞去国务院职务
“此后不久，白宫就发布了祈祷的视频和照片，”格罗布说。
他补充说：“我很快就开始收到严重关切的信息，担心我可能在全国大选前不到两周的时间里无意中参与了一场政治活动。” “我还听到一些人因为总统政策对他们或他们的家人造成的伤害而感到受伤。”
“我并不是毫无保留地去的。我希望我当时听从了他们的意见，”格罗布总结道。 “对于我的行为造成的任何损害，我深表歉意。”
总的来说，美国天主教主教会议的成员对特朗普及其政府的政策有不同的看法。例如，明尼苏达州的罗伯特·巴伦主教同意在特朗普的宗教自由委员会任职，该委员会几乎全部都是保守派基督徒。其他一些主教强烈谴责特朗普在移民执法方面的强硬立场，称这与天主教教义背道而驰。
