title_en: Iowa’s Senate rivals pitch independence from their parties
title_zh: 爱荷华州参议院竞争对手主张独立于其政党
summary: Ashley Hinson qualified her pledge to be Trump’s strongest ally, while Josh Turek praised the president’s border record.
summary_zh: 阿什利·辛森 (Ashley Hinson) 兑现了自己成为特朗普最强大盟友的承诺，而乔什·图雷克 (Josh Turek) 则赞扬了总统的边境记录。
body_en: Republican Ashley Hinson wants Iowans to know she’ll pick a fight with President Donald Trump. Democrat Josh Turek wants them to know he’ll work with him.

The rivals in Iowa’s closely contested Senate race each sought to establish their independence in separate interviews aired Sunday on ABC’s “This Week,” pitching themselves as willing to put their state ahead of their respective party loyalty.
Asked about her campaign pledge to be Trump’s “strongest ally” in the Senate, Hinson added a condition: “If it’s for Iowa.”

“I will be someone’s ally when they’re with me on the issues that are important to Iowa,” the Republican lawmaker said. “And if they’re wrong, I’m going to pick a fight with them, no matter who that is.”

The conflicting comments come in a state Trump won by 13 points in the 2024 presidential election, but where Democrats now see an opportunity to win their first Senate election since 2008. The president campaigned in Iowa this past week as high fuel costs and frustration with his tariffs complicate Republicans’ efforts to maintain the seat.
Republicans close to Hinson told POLITICO last month that she needed to put some distance between herself and Trump, warning that his tariff agenda and the Iran war were undermining her chances.
On Sunday, Hinson rejected Trump’s positive assessment of the economy. “Well, sure doesn’t feel like it right now,” she said, later criticizing the administration’s dealings with Moscow.

“I don’t think we should be making any deals with Russia,” she said, pointing to her vote for sanctions. Her campaign told POLITICO on Friday that she opposed sanctions relief for Russia while supporting Trump’s use of the Defense Production Act to bolster domestic energy production.

But there were limits to her criticism. While calling for the Iran war to end quickly, Hinson declined to oppose a potential new offensive after the midterms, saying she trusted Trump and the military to determine what needed to be done.
Turek, meanwhile, called himself a “proud moderate” and sidestepped a question about whether Democrats had moved too far left.
“I don’t think a lot about the party as a whole. I think about myself, and I think about Iowa,” the Democratic state representative said.

That pitch follows a primary victory aided by national Democratic support , including from Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s leadership PAC — which contributed the maximum to Turek’s campaign, though Schumer did not formally endorse. VoteVets spent more than $10 million advertising on Turek’s behalf. He’s also secured the formal endorsement of former President Barack Obama, who appeared in an ad alongside Turek as the two played basketball.

Asked what Trump had done right, Turek said Trump had done “a better job on the border than Biden, for sure.” He also cited agreement on keeping private equity out of housing and eliminating taxes on tips, overtime and Social Security, while arguing that Trump’s economic policies had concentrated wealth and power.
Also asked whether endorsements mattered, Turek offered a blunt assessment: “Probably not.”
body_zh: 共和党人阿什利·辛森（Ashley Hinson）希望爱荷华州人知道她会与唐纳德·特朗普总统发生争执。民主党人乔什·图雷克希望他们知道他会与他合作。
爱荷华州竞争激烈的参议院竞选中的竞争对手在美国广播公司周日播出的“本周”节目中分别接受采访时，都试图确立自己的独立性，并表示自己愿意将自己的州置于各自政党的忠诚之上。
当被问及她在竞选中承诺成为特朗普在参议院“最强大的盟友”时，辛森补充了一个条件：“如果是为了爱荷华州。”
这位共和党议员说：“当有人在对爱荷华州重要的问题上与我站在一起时，我将成为他们的盟友。” “如果他们错了，我就会和他们打架，不管他们是谁。”
这些相互矛盾的言论出现在特朗普在 2024 年总统选举中以 13 个百分点获胜的州，但民主党现在看到了赢得 2008 年以来首次参议院选举的机会。总统上周在爱荷华州进行竞选活动，因为高昂的燃油成本和对关税的不满使共和党保住席位的努力变得更加复杂。
与辛森关系密切的共和党人上个月告诉《政治》杂志，她需要与特朗普保持一定距离，并警告说，他的关税议程和伊朗战争正在削弱她的机会。
周日，辛森拒绝了特朗普对经济的积极评估。 “嗯，现在肯定不喜欢这样，”她说，后来批评了政府与莫斯科的交往。
“我认为我们不应该与俄罗斯达成任何交易，”她指着自己投票支持制裁说道。她的竞选团队周五告诉《政治》杂志，她反对放松对俄罗斯的制裁，同时支持特朗普利用《国防生产法》来促进国内能源生产。
但她的批评是有限度的。辛森在呼吁迅速结束伊朗战争的同时，拒绝反对中期选举后可能发起的新攻势，并表示她相信特朗普和军方可以决定需要做什么。
与此同时，图雷克称自己是“自豪的温和派”，并回避了民主党是否走得太左的问题。
“我对整个政党的考虑不多。我考虑的是我自己，也考虑的是爱荷华州，”这位民主党州代表说。
这次宣传是在全国民主党的支持下取得初选胜利之后进行的，其中包括参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默领导的政治行动委员会，该组织为图雷克的竞选活动做出了最大贡献，尽管舒默并未正式支持。 VoteVets 为 Turek 花费了超过 1000 万美元的广告费用。他还获得了前总统巴拉克·奥巴马的正式认可，奥巴马在两人打篮球时与图雷克一起出现在广告中。
当被问及特朗普做对了什么时，图雷克表示，特朗普“在边境方面做得比拜登更好”。他还引用了关于阻止私募股权投资住房以及取消小费、加班费和社会保障税的协议，同时认为特朗普的经济政策集中了财富和权力。
当被问及背书是否重要时，图雷克给出了直率的评价：“可能不重要。”

title_en: Why Dems’ late House reaches don’t usually pan out
title_zh: 为什么民主党在众议院后期的影响通常不会成功
summary: The DCCC has added nine candidates to its coveted "Red to Blue" support program since the beginning of September. Most face long odds.
summary_zh: 自 9 月初以来，DCCC 已为其令人垂涎的“红到蓝”支持计划增加了九名候选人。大多数人面临着很大的胜算。
body_en: House Democrats are pushing into redder and redder territory. History shows those last-minute moves don’t usually pan out, even in favorable cycles.

Since 2018, Democrats haven’t flipped any Republican-held seat that was added to the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee’s “Red to Blue” list in the September or October before Election Day, according to a POLITICO analysis. Of the 28 total candidates from 2018 to 2024 that were added in the final two months of the campaign, just three Democrats won — all in Democratic-held open seats.
That’s a much lower rate than average Red to Blue performance. Out of 203 candidates added to the program in the four previous cycles, 73 flipped their seats.

That’s not a shock: The DCCC tends to add the biggest reaches later as it moves through the cycle, both to make sure its best opportunities are funded first and have enough attention and to try to create a sense of momentum and map expansion for donors and the media.

In fact, the DCCC used some of the seats in their latest round of additions in a recent fundraising plea sent out by Executive Director Julie Merz, who warned that without more cash the committee “could be leaving winnable races on the table.”

But it illuminates how hard it is — even in the best of environments — to reach deep into red territory in order to flip House seats. And it’s especially true now, as the House battlefield has shrunk significantly since 2018 because of gerrymandering.

Since the beginning of September, the DCCC has added nine Democrats to Red to Blue: independent Bill Hill in AK-AL; Will Lawrence in MI-07; Mitchell Berman in WI-01; Chris Jones in AR-02; Dwayne Romero in CO-03; Eliott Rodriguez in FL-27; Teresa Benitez-Thompson in NV-02; Blake Gendebien in NY-21; and Justin Pearson in TN-09.

Democrats acknowledge these late additions are a low-percentage play. Former DCCC staffer Cole Leiter, who worked there for the 2018 and 2020 cycles, said the committee recruits and tracks reach-district candidates early in the cycle with hopes the political winds will shift their way.
“That is an investment in the unpredictability of the map,” Leiter said. “Most of these seats probably won’t flip, but one or two might.”

Regardless of whether or not Democrats ultimately win the seats they’ve added late this year (the DCCC added six deep-red targets to Red to Blue in early October) — the additions alone contribute to a narrative of a party on offense. And they can also be a boon for fundraising for those specific candidates as well as to entice donors with exactly which areas their dollars will go if they pony up.

“Even if there's ultimately not a massive success rate in those final editions, it is not a bad thing to make sure that those campaigns have any last-minute dollars that the designation can bring,” said Meredith Kelly, a former DCCC staffer who worked the 2016 and 2018 cycles. “Just make sure that they have a surfboard in the water and have an ability to potentially take advantage of a really, really good night.”

This cycle’s late-add Democrats are almost all facing cash disadvantages against their incumbent GOP opponents. Of the nine Democrats added within the past two months, only one — Benitez-Thompson, running against Republican David Flippo — has reported more cash on hand than their opponent. Five of them are facing fundraising deficits of over $1 million, according to Federal Election Commission filings.
Democrats’ poor record in these seats is somewhat self-selecting — seats added to the program late in the cycle reflect the fact that Democrats weren’t initially convinced they could be flipped.

Whitney Fox, who lost by 9 points to GOP Rep. Anna Paulina Luna in FL-13 in 2024 and was among the last Democrats to be added to Red to Blue when she was picked in late September, said her campaign suffered from the delay in adding her to the program, even as she acknowledged the DCCC is forced to make strategic decisions with limited resources.

The late additions also limit the window that candidates can capitalize on the program’s benefits. After initially being told she wouldn’t be added and after what she said was months of making her case to the DCCC, Fox made the list just before Hurricane Milton devastated the Tampa area, which she said made it difficult to fundraise off her newly minted Red to Blue status.
“I felt like it was too little, too late,” she said.

The Democrat running against Luna this cycle, Leela Gray, was added to Red to Blue in late August. Fox, who is informally advising local Florida candidates this cycle, said she offered Gray advice on how to make the list early.

“I was a squeaky wheel trying to talk to leadership and Democratic members of Congress, and then it got to a certain point where I was no longer the squeaky wheel,” she said she relayed to Gray. “I was going to take the spoke off the wheel and hit people over the head with it.”

Still the DCCC believes this cycle will be different, history be damned. And if recent national polling showing them with a double-digit lead in the generic ballot is correct, some of these late additions might break through.

“Records are meant to be broken,” DCCC spokesperson Viet Shelton said in a statement. “We’re on track to break them this year because across the battlefield, we’ve got amazing recruits and the enthusiasm to fire House Republicans for making life unaffordable is off the charts.”
body_zh: 众议院民主党人正在向越来越红的领域推进。历史表明，即使在有利的周期中，这些最后一刻的举动通常也不会成功。
根据 POLITICO 的分析，自 2018 年以来，民主党还没有推翻任何在选举日前 9 月或 10 月添加到民主党国会竞选委员会“红变蓝”名单中的共和党席位。 2018 年至 2024 年竞选最后两个月新增的 28 名候选人中，只有 3 名民主党人获胜——全部都是民主党占据的空缺席位。
这比红到蓝的平均性能要低得多。在前四个周期加入该计划的 203 名候选人中，有 73 人更换了席位。
这并不令人震惊：DCCC 倾向于在整个周期中后期增加最大的影响力，既是为了确保其最佳机会首先得到资助并获得足够的关注，也是为了为捐助者和媒体创造一种动力和地图扩张的感觉。
事实上，DCCC 在执行董事 Julie Merz 最近发出的筹款请求中使用了最新一轮新增席位中的一些席位，她警告说，如果没有更多现金，委员会“可能会将可获胜的比赛留在桌面上”。
但它表明，即使在最好的环境下，深入红色领域以翻转众议院席位也是多么困难。现在尤其如此，因为自 2018 年以来，由于选区不公正，众议院战场已大幅缩小。

自 9 月初以来，DCCC 已将 9 名民主党人加入红蓝阵营：AK-AL 的独立人士 Bill Hill； 《MI-07》中的威尔·劳伦斯； WI-01 中的米切尔·伯曼； AR-02 中的克里斯·琼斯； CO-03 中的德韦恩·罗梅罗； FL-27 中的艾略特·罗德里格斯；特雷莎·贝尼特斯-汤普森 NV-02； NY-21 中的布莱克·根德比恩 (Blake Gendebien)；和 TN-09 中的贾斯汀·皮尔森。
民主党人承认这些后期添加的内容比例较低。曾在 2018 年和 2020 年周期工作过的前 DCCC 工作人员科尔·莱特 (Cole Leiter) 表示，该委员会在周期初期招募并跟踪覆盖地区的候选人，希望政治风向能够改变方向。
“这是对地图不可预测性的投资，”莱特说。 “这些座位中的大多数可能不会翻转，但一两个可能会翻转。”
无论民主党最终是否赢得今年年底增加的席位（DCCC 于 10 月初在“红到蓝”中增加了六个深红色目标）——仅这些增加就有助于描述一个政党进攻的情况。它们还可以为那些特定候选人筹集资金，并通过捐助者确切地知道他们的钱将用于哪些领域来吸引捐助者。
曾在 2016 年和 2018 年周期工作的前 DCCC 工作人员梅雷迪思·凯利 (Meredith Kelly) 表示：“即使这些最终版本最终没有取得巨大成功，但确保这些活动能够在最后一刻获得指定所能带来的资金，也不是什么坏事。” “只要确保他们在水中有冲浪板，并且有能力度过一个非常非常美好的夜晚即可。”
本周期后期的民主党人几乎都面临着与现任共和党对手相比的现金劣势。在过去两个月内增加的九名民主党人中，只有一位—​​—贝尼特斯·汤普森（Benitez-Thompson），与共和党人大卫·弗利波(David Flippo)竞争——报告手头现金比对手多。根据联邦选举委员会的文件，其中 5 家面临超过 100 万美元的筹款赤字。
民主党在这些席位上的糟糕记录在某种程度上是自我选择的——在周期后期添加到该计划的席位反映出民主党最初并不相信自己可以被推翻。
惠特尼·福克斯 (Whitney Fox) 在 2024 年 FL-13 选举中以 9 个百分点的优势输给了共和党众议员安娜·宝琳娜·卢纳 (Anna Paulina Luna)，她是 9 月底被选中时最后一批加入红蓝计划的民主党人之一。惠特尼·福克斯表示，她的竞选活动因将她加入该计划的延迟而受到影响，尽管她承认 DCCC 被迫在资源有限的情况下做出战略决策。
最新增加的内容也限制了候选人可以利用该计划优势的窗口。最初被告知她不会被列入名单，并且据她所说，在向 DCCC 陈述了几个月的时间后，福克斯在飓风米尔顿摧毁坦帕地区之前进入了名单，她说这使得她很难为她新获得的从红到蓝的地位筹集资金。
“我觉得这太少了，也太晚了，”她说。
本轮与 Luna 竞选的民主党人 Leela Gray 于 8 月底被加入红蓝阵营。福克斯在本周期为佛罗里达州当地候选人提供非正式建议，她说她向格雷提供了如何尽早入围的建议。
“我是一个吱吱作响的轮子，试图与领导层和国会民主党议员交谈，然后到了一定程度，我不再是吱吱作响的轮子，”她说她转述给格雷。 “我要把辐条从方向盘上取下来，用它打人的头。”
尽管如此，DCCC 仍相信，无论历史如何，这个周期将会有所不同。如果最近的全国民意调查显示他们在通用选票中领先两位数是正确的，那么其中一些后来增加的人可能会突破。
DCCC 发言人 Viet Shelton 在一份声明中表示：“记录就是用来打破的。” “今年我们有望打破这些限制，因为在战场的另一边，我们拥有出色的新兵，并且解雇那些让生活变得难以负担的众议院共和党人的热情是空前的。”

Up First briefing: GOP redistricting; France, Serbia protests; Brazil election Republicans are spending millions on the midterms, and they still may not win districts drawn to favor them. And, Brazil's Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term in a stunning political comeback.

Redistricting isn't playing out how the GOP hoped. And, Brazil's Lula wins 4th term
GOP Redistricting Bust, Lula Wins Brazil Election, Protest Spread In Europe

North Carolina Republican Congressional candidates, State Rep. Jennifer Balkcom and Laurie Buckhout (R) are embraced by President Trump during an election rally on October 20, 2026 in Greenville, North Carolina. Buckhout is running in North Carolina's 1st District which was redrawn to heavily favor Republicans and is now a toss-up. Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images hide caption

Republicans had a plan to keep control of the House in the midterms: Redraw congressional district lines to favor the GOP and avoid the historical pattern of heavy midterm losses. President Trump began pressuring Republican-led states to do just that last year, but it isn't working out as expected. Republicans could now be spending millions of dollars on House seats that were supposed to be easy wins, and end up losing anyway . Of the 15 districts drawn specifically to favor Republicans, only five are rated by the Cook Political Report as either likely or solid Republican. Most are toss-ups or lean toward a Democratic win.

🎧 One reason the Republicans' redistricting push hasn't been as successful as expected is that some district lines were drawn based on the 2024 Trump electorate, NPR's Tamara Keith tells Up First . Since then, his support has weakened , particularly among young and Latino voters. Several Democratic incumbents targeted by redistricting have stuck it out to fight for their seats. A Republican strategist involved with midterm races, but who wasn't authorized to speak publicly, pushed back on the characterization that redistricting didn't work, saying that it "creates new battlefields" but doesn't "create outcomes."

In a stunning political comeback, leftist Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in the presidential runoff election in Brazil. Lula defeated Flávio Bolsonaro , son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, by more than 4 million votes. It's the first time since Brazil restored democracy in 1989 that a candidate who finished second in the first round has gone on to win the presidency.

🎧 Lula's win appears to have put the brake on a right-wing sweep in Latin America, NPR's Carrie Kahn says. Seven conservative presidents have been elected in the past 18 months. Kahn says one message helped rally voters in the final weeks of Lula's campaign: that the return of a Bolsonaro to power would be an existential threat to Brazilian democracy.

Large demonstrations against the government continued over the weekend in France, where more than 100,000 people showed up in Paris, and more than 400,000 came out nationwide. What started with students demanding better conditions has grown into a much bigger movement. Unions and public-sector workers have joined, calling for more public spending and protesting growing inequality. Similar protests have erupted across Europe, from Spain to Serbia.

🎧 The reasons behind the protests vary, from schools and housing costs to corruption, NPR's Eleanor Beardsley says. But they have something in common: most are leaderless movements by young people frustrated with the world they're being left to. In Serbia, crowds celebrated in the streets of Belgrade after a student-led movement known as the "student-list" defeated the party of longtime strongman Aleksandar Vucic in Sunday's parliamentary elections. The win followed two years of protests over government corruption and lack of accountability.

Out-of-pocket maternity expenses are difficult to predict. A federal requirement for insurers to provide personalized cost estimates under the No Surprises Act was supposed to take effect in 2022, but federal regulators haven't made it happen despite pressure from Congress. Until the cost of maternity care gets more transparent, here are some tips to help you budget for the cost of pregnancy
👶 Enroll your baby in your insurance before your deadline. For most employer health plans, that's within 30 days of birth.
👶 Check what your maximum out-of-pocket expense is. That's the most you'll pay each year for covered, in-network expenses before your insurance pays 100% of the costs.
👶 Choose in-network providers whenever possible.
👶 Go over every bill, and don't be afraid to appeal errors.
👶 Ask your hospital or other providers about financial assistance.

北卡罗来纳州共和党国会候选人、州众议员詹妮弗·巴尔克科姆 (Jennifer Balkcom) 和劳里·巴克豪特 (Laurie Buckhout)（右）于 2026 年 10 月 20 日在北卡罗来纳州格林维尔举行的选举集会上受到特朗普总统的拥抱。巴克豪特在北卡罗来纳州第一选区竞选，该选区经过重新划定以大力支持共和党，现在是一个难以预测的局面。安娜摇钱树/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏

共和党人有一个在中期选举中保持对众议院控制权的计划：重新划定国会选区界限以支持共和党，并避免中期选举惨败的历史模式。特朗普总统去年开始向共和党领导的各州施压，要求他们这样做，但效果并不如预期。共和党人现在可能会花费数百万美元来赢得本应轻松获胜的众议院席位，但无论如何最终都会失败。在专门为共和党选区的 15 个选区中，只有 5 个选区被库克政治报告评为可能或坚定的共和党人。大多数都是犹豫不决或倾向于民主党获胜。

🎧 NPR 的塔玛拉·基思 (Tamara Keith) 告诉 Up First，共和党的选区重划行动没有像预期那样成功的原因之一是，一些选区划分是根据 2024 年特朗普选民的情况绘制的。从那时起，他的支持率有所减弱，特别是在年轻和拉丁裔选民中。几位成为选区重新划分目标的民主党现任议员坚持不懈地争取席位。一位参与中期选举但未被授权公开发言的共和党战略家反驳了选区重新划分不起作用的说法，称这“创造了新的战场”，但并没有“创造结果”。
➡️ NPR 应用程序将 NPR 的所有选举报道集中在一个地方 - 从全国最大的新闻到与家庭息息相关的问题。浏览头条新闻、播放列表、播客剧集、视频等，所有这些都在 2026 年选举选项卡上。
左翼人士路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦在巴西总统决选中赢得了第四个任期，取得了惊人的政治复兴。卢拉以超过 400 万票击败了前极右翼总统雅伊尔·博尔索纳罗的儿子弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗。这是自1989年巴西恢复民主以来，首次由在第一轮中获得第二名的候选人最终赢得总统宝座。
NPR 的卡丽·卡恩 (Carrie Kahn) 表示，卢拉的胜利似乎给右翼在拉丁美洲的横扫踩下了刹车。过去 18 个月内选出了 7 位保守派总统。卡恩表示，在卢拉竞选的最后几周，有一条信息帮助团结了选民：博尔索纳罗重新掌权将对巴西民主构成生存威胁。

Large demonstrations against the government continued over the weekend in France, where more than 100,000 people showed up in Paris, and more than 400,000 came out nationwide.最初的学生要求更好的条件已经发展成为一场更大的运动。工会和公共部门工人也加入进来，呼吁增加公共支出并抗议日益严重的不平等。从西班牙到塞尔维亚，欧洲各地都爆发了类似的抗议活动。

🎧 NPR 的埃莉诺·比尔兹利 (Eleanor Beardsley) 表示，抗议背后的原因各不相同，从学校和住房成本到腐败。但它们有一些共同点：大多数都是由对自己所处的世界感到沮丧的年轻人发起的无领导运动。在塞尔维亚，学生领导的名为“学生名单”的运动在周日的议会选举中击败了长期强人亚历山大·武契奇的政党后，人群在贝尔格莱德街头庆祝。这场胜利是在针对政府腐败和缺乏问责制的抗议活动进行了两年之后取得的。
自付费用的生育费用很难预测。根据《无意外法案》，联邦政府要求保险公司提供个性化成本估算，本应于 2022 年生效，但联邦监管机构尽管受到国会的压力，仍未实现这一目标。在产妇护理费用变得更加透明之前，这里有一些提示可以帮助您预算怀孕费用
👶 在截止日期之前为您的宝宝加入保险。对于大多数雇主健康计划来说，这是在出生后 30 天内。
👶 检查您的最大自付费用是多少。这是您每年在保险支付 100% 费用之前为承保的网络内费用支付的最高金额。
👶 尽可能选择网络内提供商。
👶 仔细检查每一份账单，不要害怕对错误提出上诉。

body_en: Authorities launch manhunt for convicted killer who escaped Tennessee prison
Authorities in Tennessee launched an intense manhunt for a convicted murderer who escaped from a state prison, allegedly stole a work truck and remains on the loose.

Jacob Allen Morley, 28, escaped from the state’s Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville sometime before he was reported as missing at 11:30 p.m. Sunday, prison officials said in a statement Monday.
“Further review of security cameras confirmed Morley breached the perimeter fence and exited the facility in his TDOC uniform,” the Tennessee Department of Correction said in a statement.
By 1 a.m. Monday, he allegedly stole a white, Ford F-350 flatbed truck in the city of about 3,500, some 100 miles north of Memphis, state law enforcement and corrections officials said.

Tiptonville is near the Mississippi River and its state line with Missouri. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation placed Morley on its most-wanted list and asked residents of the city to check any video they may have for possible footage of the convict.
“Residents are urged to check home security systems, including doorbell cameras and trail cameras, for any sightings of Morley or the stolen truck,” the bureau said in a statement.

Security video of the alleged truck theft shows a man in a beanie walk around the rear of the vehicle to the driver’s side door. It then shows the truck’s windshield wipers moving before the truck is driven away.
Morley is 5 feet, 11 inches tall and weighs 240 pounds, the Tennessee Department of Correction said.
It said a reward of up to $2,500 is available to anyone who has information leading to the fugitive’s capture.
Anyone who sees the convict was asked to immediately call 911 or 1-800-TBI-FIND.

Morley fatally shot his coworker, 34-year-old Cody Birchfield, in the back of the head in 2022, according to court documents shared by the Carter County Clerk’s Office. Birchfield’s body was found in a large metal box under Morley’s residence, the documents state.
Morley was convicted in February 2025 and sentenced to life behind bars.
He was also convicted of abuse of a corpse, tampering with evidence, and aggravated burglary — the latter for stealing tools from the victim, according to the court documents.
Morley was described at trial as a “loner,” the clerk’s office said. He claimed self-defense and said he had mental health issues, including bipolar disorder.

body_en: OpenAI announces three big science discoveries and a new way to work with academics
This time OpenAI says it’s taking new advice from scientists on how to release the results.
All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
Richard Lawler is a senior editor following news across tech, culture, policy, and entertainment. He joined The Verge in 2021 after several years covering news at Engadget.

Less than a month after its mass release of hundreds of manuscripts that it said contained solutions to long-standing mathematics questions, OpenAI is back with three more “major” discoveries in math, computer science, and physics . What’s different this time is the choice to have external experts that OpenAI describes as “shepherds” guiding the results in computer science and physics, while for the math problem it says that they advised it to release the AI output for researchers to work through their own explanations.

Local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation. The proof uses an auxiliary partial differential equation to establish Sogge’s local smoothing for waves in every spatial dimension at least two. It also yields the Kakeya maximal and dimension conjectures and Stein’s spherical restriction estimates throughout the interior of the conjectured range. We are releasing the model output directly, as we did in our October 6 release.

The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False. The paper gives a deterministic algorithm that exactly counts satisfying assignments of fixed-width CNF formulas in subexponential time and polynomial space. The case of 3-SAT refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis. An independent working group of computer scientists led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi, and Ryan Williams will examine and explain the proof. At the group’s request, we are making the materials public immediately so others can examine them as well.

This approach could have its own issues, the company admits, and the AGMAI panel of math advisers OpenAI put together just said yesterday that “we recommend that AI companies do not adopt” the practices of designating certain people to receive the output first, citing unequal access, borrowed reputation, and biased selection as a few of the issues. Instead, they recommended that in the future, AI labs release output on scholarly repositories, with Lean-formalized proofs, info on how the problems were chosen, funding for people working on understanding the results, and other information.
‘Pure insanity’: Mathematicians will need years to make sense of OpenAI’s latest drop

The physics information has not been released in full, but is a “mathematically rigorous existence proof of certain interacting quantum field theories containing gauge fields and fermions in four dimensions, including Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and a unified completion of the Standard Model of particle physics.” According to OpenAI, “David Gross will lead a group including Michael Douglas, Arthur Jaffe, Igor Klebanov, and Nikita Nekrasov that will shepherd this work.”

The computer science collaboration is said to prove that the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH) , which has been widely believed to be true, is actually false. OpenAI says verification of the result will be guided by a group of three experts that includes UC San Diego’s Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, who were part of the group that originally proposed it in 1999 , as well as MIT professor Ryan Williams . The group decided to release the AI output write-up and Lean proof on GitHub today .
They also released an open letter to the community asking for input on how to examine the claim, and about setting norms for dealing with AI-generated breakthroughs
We would welcome discussion of three broader questions
What expectations should govern early access to AI-generated results, disclosure of conflicts of interest, and the use of unpublished material for subsequent research?
How should credit recognize both new discoveries and the work of checking, fixing, simplifying, explaining, and extending them?
How can we support students and researchers as methods and research directions change, while preserving the understanding and judgment needed to question results and develop new ideas?

There’s similar documentation for the math breakthrough, where its model “produced a proof of the local smoothing conjecture in every dimension and therefore also resolve the Kakeya conjecture and Stein’s restriction conjecture in all dimensions.” Just a few months ago, NYU professor Hong Wang was awarded a prestigious Fields Medal by the International Mathematical Union for resolving the Kakeya conjecture in three dimensions.

body_zh: OpenAI 宣布三项重大科学发现以及与学术界合作的新方式
这次 OpenAI 表示，它正在听取科学家关于如何发布结果的新建议。
所有围绕人工智能接管数学的戏剧
理查德·劳勒 (Richard Lawler) 是一名高级编辑，关注科技、文化、政策和娱乐领域的新闻。在 Engadget 报道新闻几年后，他于 2021 年加入 The Verge。
OpenAI 大规模发布数百份手稿（据称这些手稿包含了长期存在的数学问题的解决方案）不到一个月，又在数学、计算机科学和物理学领域带来了三项“重大”发现。这次的不同之处在于，选择让 OpenAI 称之为“牧羊人”的外部专家来指导计算机科学和物理学的结果，而对于数学问题，OpenAI 表示，他们建议 OpenAI 发布人工智能输出，供研究人员进行自己的解释。
欧几里德波动方程的局部平滑。该证明使用辅助偏微分方程来建立索格对每个空间维度至少为 2 的波的局部平滑。它还产生了挂谷极大猜想和维数猜想以及整个猜想范围内部的斯坦因球形限制估计。我们将直接发布模型输出，就像我们在 10 月 6 日发布的版本中所做的那样。
指数时间假说是错误的。论文给出了一种确定性算法，可以精确计算次指数时间和多项式空间中固定宽度 CNF 公式的满足赋值。 3-SAT 的案例反驳了指数时间假说。由 Russell Impagliazzo、Ramamohan Paturi 和 Ryan Williams 领导的一个由计算机科学家组成的独立工作组将检查并解释该证明。应该组织的要求，我们立即公开这些材料，以便其他人也可以检查它们。
该公司承认，这种方法可能有其自身的问题，OpenAI 组成的 AGMAI 数学顾问小组昨天刚刚表示，“我们建议人工智能公司不要采用”指定某些人首先接收输出的做法，并指出了不平等的访问权、借来的声誉和有偏见的选择等问题。相反，他们建议未来人工智能实验室在学术存储库上发布成果，其中包括精益形式化证明、有关如何选择问题的信息、为致力于理解结果的人员提供资金以及其他信息。
“纯粹的疯狂”：数学家需要数年时间才能理解 OpenAI 的最新跌幅
这些物理信息尚未完全公开，但它是“某些包含规范场和四维费米子相互作用的量子场论的数学严格存在证明，包括量子色动力学（QCD）和粒子物理标准模型的统一完成。”据 OpenAI 称，“David Gross 将领导一个由 Michael Douglas、Arthur Jaffe、Igor Klebanov 和 Nikita Nekrasov 组成的团队来领导这项工作。”

据说，计算机科学合作证明了被广泛认为正确的指数时间假说（ETH）实际上是错误的。 OpenAI 表示，结果的验证将由三名专家组成的小组指导，其中包括加州大学圣地亚哥分校的 Russell Impagliazzo 和 Ramamohan Paturi（他们是 1999 年最初提出该结果的小组的成员），以及麻省理工学院教授 Ryan Williams。该小组决定今天在 GitHub 上发布人工智能输出文章和精益证明。
他们还向社区发布了一封公开信，征求有关如何审查这一主张以及制定处理人工智能突破的规范的意见
我们欢迎讨论三个更广泛的问题
对于人工智能生成的结果的早期获取、利益冲突的披露以及后续研究中未发表材料的使用，应该有哪些期望？
信用应该如何认可新发现以及检查、修复、简化、解释和扩展这些发现的工作？
随着方法和研究方向的变化，我们如何支持学生和研究人员，同时保留质疑结果和发展新想法所需的理解和判断？
对于数学突破也有类似的文档，其模型“在每个维度上都产生了局部平滑猜想的证明，因此也解决了在所有维度上的挂谷猜想和斯坦因限制猜想。”就在几个月前，纽约大学教授王宏因解决了三维挂谷猜想而被国际数学联盟授予享有盛誉的菲尔兹奖。
